title: Operator
content: We'll go next to Justin Post with Bank of America Merrill Lynch.

speaker: Justin Post
title: Analyst
content: I have two questions. First, can you discuss your expectations for AWS? Do you believe its growth trajectory can match that of your retail business, and what do you anticipate regarding its margin profile compared to your core business? Secondly, have you revised the historical forecast for third-party units? I noticed that some of the past figures may have been higher than what you previously reported in a few prior quarters.

speaker: Thomas Szkutak
title: CFO
content: I'll address the second question first. Regarding unit growth and third-party units, this quarter we opted to focus on paid unit growth rather than total units, which is a shift from our previous approach that included a number of free units. For instance, in the current quarter, we reported a paid unit growth of 56%. In comparison, the paid unit growth was 45% in Q1. The Q1 figure we shared was actually 51% because it included free units. So, the 45% for Q1 and the 56% for Q2 are comparable since they both reflect paid units. Additionally, the percentage of total units from third parties was 36% this quarter, an increase from 34% last year. Again, this percentage refers to paid units relative to total units. We thought it would be useful to present this perspective this quarter. As for the AWS business, it's definitely a massive sector. While it's difficult to predict how substantial it will become for Amazon, we are extremely enthusiastic about this business. The team has done an excellent job and continues to innovate for our customers. We have a fantastic group of innovators and operators managing that business, and we are very excited about its future.

speaker: Justin Post
title: Analyst
content: Can you say whether it's in investment mode or is it contributing at all to the bottom line at this point?

speaker: Thomas Szkutak
title: CFO
content: You should expect that we continue to invest in that business because of the high-growth nature of it. It's growing very fast. It is one of the reasons why you're seeing certainly a big contributor to our CapEx. It's also reflected in the tech and content line. And so again we're very excited about what we're seeing there. And the team is going to continue to stay heads down focused on their customer to drive that business.

speaker: John Felton
title: Director of Investor Relations

speaker: John Felton
title: Director of Investor Relations
content: Hello, and welcome to our Q3 2011 Financial Results Conference Call. Joining us today is Tom Szkutak, our CFO. We will be available for questions after our prepared remarks. During this call, we will discuss certain non-GAAP financial measures. In our press release, slides accompanying this webcast and our filings with the SEC, each of which is posted on our IR website, you will find additional disclosures regarding these non-GAAP measures, including reconciliations of these measures with comparable GAAP measures. speaker: Thomas J. Szkutak
title: CFO
content: Thanks, John. I'll begin with comments on our third quarter financial results. Trailing 12-month operating cash flow increased 19% to $3.11 billion. Trailing 12-month free cash flow decreased 17% to $1.53 billion. Return on invested capital is 17%, down from 28%. The combination of common stock and stock-based awards outstanding was 469 million shares compared with 465 million shares. Worldwide revenue grew 44% to $10.88 billion or 39%, excluding the $371 million favorable impact from year-over-year changes in foreign exchange. We are grateful to our customers who continue to take advantage of our low prices, vast selection, and shipping offers. Media revenue increased to $4.15 billion, up 24% or 19%, excluding foreign exchange. EGM revenue increased to $6.32 billion, up 59% or 54%, excluding foreign exchange. Worldwide EGM increased to 58% of worldwide sales, up from 53%. Worldwide paid unit growth was 53%. Active customer accounts exceeded 152 million. Worldwide active sellers were more than 2 million. Now I'll discuss operating expenses, excluding stock-based compensation. Cost of sales was $8.32 billion or 76.5% of revenue consistent with the prior-year period. Fulfillment, marketing, technology and content, and G&A combined was $2.29 billion or 21.1% of sales, up approximately 290 basis points year-over-year. Fulfillment was $1.09 billion or 10% of revenue compared with 8.7%. Tech and content was $694 million or 6.4% of revenue compared with 5.1%. Marketing was $360 million or 3.3% of revenue compared with 3.1%. Now I'll talk about our segment results, and consistent with prior periods, we do not allocate segments or stock-based type of compensation or other operating expense line item. In the North American segment, revenue grew 44% to $5.93 billion. Media revenue grew 21% to $1.93 billion. EGM revenue grew 56% to $3.64 billion, representing 51% of North American revenues, up from 56%. North America segment operating income decreased 23% to $144 million, a 2.4% operating margin. In the International segment, revenue grew 44% to $4.94 billion, adjusting for the $367 million year-over-year favorable foreign exchange impact, revenue growth was 33%. Media revenue grew 27% to $2.23 billion or 17% excluding foreign exchange and EGM revenue grew 63% to $2.68 million or 51%, excluding foreign exchange. EGM now represents 54% of international revenues up from 48%. International segment operating income decreased 46% to $116 million, a 2.4% operating margin. Excluding the favorable impact of foreign exchange, International segment operating income decreased 55%. Consolidated segment operating income decreased 35% to $260 million or 2.4% of revenue down approximately 290 basis points year-over-year. Excluding the $14 million favorable impact from foreign exchange, CSOI decreased 38%. Unlike CSOI, our GAAP operating income includes stock-based compensation expense and other operating expense. GAAP operating income decreased 71% to $79 million or 0.7% of net sales. Our income tax expense was $67 million in Q3, resulting in a 52% rate for the quarter and a 31% rate year-to-date. GAAP net income was $63 million or $0.14 per diluted share compared with $231 million and $0.51 per diluted share. Turning to the balance sheet. Cash and marketable securities increased $441 million year-over-year to $6.33 billion. Inventory increased 50% to $3.77 billion and inventory turns were 10.8, down from 11.8 turns a year ago, as we expanded selection, improved in-stock levels and introduced new product categories. Accounts payable increased 42% to $6.55 billion and accounts payable days decreased to 72 from 73 in the prior year. Our Q3 2011 capital expenditures were $529 million. The increase in capital expenditures reflects additional investments in support of continued business growth, including investments in technology infrastructure, including Amazon Web Services and capacity to support our fulfillment operations. I'll conclude my portion of today's call with guidance. Incorporated into the guidance are the trends that we've seen to date and what we believe today to be appropriately conservative assumptions. Our results are inherently unpredictable and may be materially affected by many factors, including a high level of uncertainty surrounding exchange rate fluctuations, as well as the global economy and consumer spending. It's not possible to accurately predict demand. Therefore, our actual results could differ materially from our guidance. As we describe in more detail in our public filings, issues such as settling inter-company balances in foreign currencies amongst our subsidiaries, unfavorable resolution of legal matters, and changes to our effective tax rates can all have a material effect on guidance. Our guidance further assumes that we don't conclude any additional business acquisitions or investments, record any further revisions to stock-based compensation estimates, and that foreign exchange rates remain approximately where they've been recently. For Q4 2011, we expect net sales between $16.45 billion and $18.65 billion, or growth between 27% and 44%. This guidance anticipates approximately 130 basis points of favorable impact from foreign exchange. GAAP operating income or loss to be between a $200 million loss and $250 million of income, or between a 142% decline and 47% decline. This includes approximately $200 million for stock-based compensation and amortization of intangible assets. We anticipate consolidated segment operating income, which excludes stock-based compensation and other operating expenses, to be between $0 and $450 million or between a 100% decline and 28% decline. We remain heads down focused on driving a better customer experience through price selection and convenience. We believe putting customers first is the only reliable way to create lasting value for shareholders. Thanks. And with that, John, let's move to questions.

speaker: John Felton
title: Director of Investor Relations

title: Operator

title: Analyst

speaker: Thomas J. Szkutak
title: CFO
content: Sure. In terms of the guidance for revenue for Q4, as we've done in previous years, we've given a wide range of guidance in Q4 just because of the seasonality and it's difficult to predict. But we feel very good about the demand that we've seen to date. And certainly, at the high end of the guidance, you can see there's an acceleration that's possible reflected in that guidance. But we are given a wide range consistent with what we've done in prior Q4s. In terms of the overall growth that we've seen so far, you saw a very strong growth in Q3, up 39% on a local currency basis. That's consistent with what we've seen over the past 12 months where we're up 39%, also over the trailing 12 months. And we really saw a step change 2 years ago where we saw year-over-year growth up 39%. So again, we feel very good about the growth that we are experiencing, and I've seen data reflected in the guidance given a wide range. In terms of Kindle Fire in our guidance and certainly the largest portion of that would be reflected in our revenue.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: We'll go next to Youssef Squali with Jefferies & Company.

speaker: Youssef H. Squali
title: Analyst
content: Tom, can you explain what's putting pressure on margins in the third and fourth quarters? I assume the margin forecast for the fourth quarter is essentially at zero at the midpoint. This raises the question of our financial model going forward: are we aiming to maximize growth on the top line even if it means having zero margin?

speaker: Thomas J. Szkutak
title: CFO
content: We're experiencing significant growth, the best we've seen since 2000, especially over the past 12 months ending in September. With this robust growth, we are investing heavily in capacity, which we’ve discussed over the past few quarters and is reflected in our Q3 results. If you examine our operating expenses in Q3 as a percentage of revenue and compare them to Q2, you’ll notice similar trends in marketing and general and administrative expenses. There’s a slight increase in technology costs, about 10 basis points, and fulfillment costs are up around 80 basis points. The rise in fulfillment costs as a percentage of revenue is tied to the capacity investments we’ve mentioned. Recently, I noted that we announced 15 new fulfillment centers this year compared to 52 last year, and we plan to open one or two more, bringing the total to 17 new centers. This is impacting our fulfillment expenses in Q3 as well as our bottom line. We are also investing across various areas including support for retail and Amazon fulfillment growth, our rapidly growing AWS business, and infrastructure for our retail operations. We're making investments in our Kindle and Digital business, which will be reflected in our Q4 guidance. For instance, we launched four new Kindle products at the end of September that we are very excited about due to their competitive pricing and premium quality. We consider the overall economics of the Kindle business, including the lifetime value of the devices and content, as well as sales of Special Offers devices that include advertisements. All these investments are influencing our Q4 guidance, but we are optimistic about our current position and prospective opportunities.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: We'll take our next question from Scott Devitt with Morgan Stanley.

speaker: Scott W. Devitt
title: Analyst
content: Tom, just a bigger picture question on the Retail business. Just wondering given some of the emerging markets and the competitive landscape that's occurring, particularly in Asia. How do you think about that?

speaker: Thomas J. Szkutak
title: CFO
content: Sure. To take a step back, whenever we enter a new geography or category, we aim to ensure that we can add value. For instance, we prefer categories with many different SKUs that are complex in physical retail settings. We also seek categories where we believe we can enhance value from a service perspective. In every category we operate in, we strive to ensure that we can achieve great returns on invested capital over time. While I may not be directly answering your question, we assess this on a category-by-category basis and focus on where we can make an impact. Historically, you can see that as we have entered new categories and geographies, we have always prioritized the customer. Initially, we often expand selection from a retail standpoint, sometimes including third parties from the start or adding them later on. We believe this approach has served us well, and we continually seek ways to provide greater value for both customers and shareholders over time.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: Next, we'll go to Jim Friedland with Cowen and Company.

speaker: James H. Friedland
title: Analyst
content: I wanted to ask about Netflix launching in the U.K. and Ireland with streaming. You bought Lovefilm earlier in the year, but it doesn't seem like the streaming side of the business has changed much. Are there any plans to increase investment in content outside the U.S., beyond what you're doing with Prime streaming? Also, regarding Quidsi, we've seen numerous new announcements related to new brands and categories. Is this significantly affecting some of the lower operating profits? Is Quidsi just not large enough as a percentage of total to make a difference?

speaker: Thomas J. Szkutak
title: CFO
content: In terms of Lovefilm, we have been investing in content since the acquisition and will continue to do so. We believe it's a great opportunity, and the business is performing well. We're pleased with the team's efforts and excited about the prospects ahead. As for Quidsi, they are continuing to expand and doing a good job. This will be reflected in the guidance we are providing for Q4, but I wouldn’t consider it to have a material impact.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: We'll take our next question from Ross Sandler with RBC Capital Markets.

speaker: Ross Sandler
title: Analyst
content: Just two quick questions. First on U.S. EGM, there was a bit more deceleration there than prior quarters. I know that comp was more challenging, but can you give us a little color on what's going on with the deceleration in domestic EGM? And then a question on mobile, our smart phone and tablet users that are buying physical goods on the Amazon mobile app, how does their purchase behavior differ from the same users who are buying stuff on PC? Are they buying more physical goods or less, not ebooks or digital goods, but just specifically physical goods?

speaker: Thomas J. Szkutak
title: CFO
content: Sure. In terms of the first part of your question, we are very pleased with the growth rate we saw in North America EGM. It was up 56% year-over-year. And you do have it right. It is a bit of a tough compare if you look back to last year. We did grow 80%. It was certainly a high watermark for us and we're overlapping that. We had very, very strong growth last year Q3. But again, still very pleased with what we see in Q3 of this year in EGM specifically and our overall growth rates too. In terms of mobile, we actually haven't released a lot of details and that's not much I can help you with there. But certainly, we are seeing good trends in our mobile business. And again, we like what we're seeing there, but there's not much I can help you with that particular question.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: We'll go next to Jeetil Patel from Deutsche Bank Securities.

speaker: Jeetil J. Patel
title: Analyst
content: I have a couple of questions. First, regarding lifetime value, can you discuss if the lifetime value of Kindle customers is comparable to or higher than that of your core retail customers? Are there specific markets or international areas that are experiencing a larger increase in third-party business?

speaker: Thomas J. Szkutak
title: CFO
content: To answer your first question, we’re not differentiating between Kindle customers and non-Kindle customers, but I can share some insights about the Kindle customer dynamics. We have gained a lot of knowledge since launching Kindle. When a customer buys the device, they tend to buy more content as well. Recently, we launched special offers and ad-based Kindles, which provided us with additional data that we didn’t have before. We’ve observed that once customers have a Kindle, they have access to a vast selection of content, which leads to more purchases. We have discussed this in previous calls. When considering lifetime value, we focus specifically on the device itself, aiming to provide the best device and content for our customers. We evaluate the overall economics, including the device, accessories, content, ad-based revenue, and special offers. We are optimistic about what we see in this area. As we approach Q4, we anticipate a record quarter for device sales. Given the timing of the sales, you can expect that content and ad revenue will follow behind the device sales. These are essential considerations for our Kindle business. We are very enthusiastic about our electronic ink and fire devices, and we believe they will ultimately benefit our shareholders. Regarding the third-party business, we are pleased with performance, as third-party units now represent 38% of total paid units this quarter, up from 35% last year. Additionally, we see strong overall unit growth, which is encouraging. This trend of robust retail growth alongside third-party growth has been evident for several years, supported by fulfillment services like Amazon.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: We'll go next to Spencer Wang with Credit Suisse.

title: Analyst

title: CFO

This content will be included in our Q4 results. Additionally, we have content costs related to Lovefilm in Europe, which are also factored into our guidance for the quarter. While we are not disclosing the specific dollar amount for these costs, they will certainly affect our overall guidance, along with our investment in the Kindle business and other initiatives I mentioned. We're excited about these opportunities and the impact they will have.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: And we'll go next to Ben Schachter with Macquarie Group.

speaker: Benjamin A. Schachter
title: Analyst
content: My understanding is that Google will be the default search engine for the Kindle Fire. Could you provide any updates on that and consider deploying devices like a Roku box directly to Prime customers for accessing video content?

speaker: Thomas J. Szkutak
title: CFO
content: It'll be very easy on Fire to access all of our digital content at first. So it's a very integrated device. It's something that we've been working on. It's coming together over a long period of time, in terms of being able to offer just a vast amount of paid and free content. In the case of video, we'll certainly have book content, music content. So it will be very easy and very integrated being able to access all of our digital content. It'll also be easy to access physical products as well. So those are things that we're very excited about, and customers will be able to see when they receive their Fire. And so we think it's an incredible product. We're very excited about it. It's certainly a premium product. And at $1.99, it's certainly not a premium price. We're very happy to offer that to customers. title: CFO

Our dedicated global team has been working hard to ensure everything is operational and that all associates are trained. To prepare for fulfillment, we are onboarding staff well in advance and securing leases and products for shipment ahead of time. However, there will be some downtime during the ramp-up period where we have personnel in the facilities, receiving products but not yet generating output. The time it takes to reach full operational capacity will vary based on the automation level of each center. We are experienced in this process, and we are confident in deploying these assets effectively to achieve strong returns on investment in the long run.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator

title: Analyst

speaker: Thomas J. Szkutak
title: CFO

Although it's still early in the process, we plan to enhance these offerings significantly over the next year, and we are optimistic about their potential. We are closely monitoring all customer metrics and evaluating the economic aspects, and while it is still in its infancy, we are encouraged by the results so far.

title: Operator

speaker: Thomas J. Szkutak
title: CFO
content: In terms of the user interface, I don't have much to add. The most recent data to consider is our Q3 results. We did not have the new user interface fully operational for the entire quarter, yet we experienced a strong growth rate in Q3, with an increase of 39%. We are optimistic about this and it is reflected in our actual results and guidance. Looking ahead to Q4, we have significantly expanded our selection over the past 12 months, offering many unique items, which positions us well for the upcoming quarter. We are ensuring that our prices remain competitive to provide great value to our customers. We are also committed to improving our service levels in various ways, with timely delivery being crucial, and our increased number of Prime members this year is essential to that effort. We have four new Kindle products available at attractive prices. All these factors prepare us for a strong growth quarter in Q4. We remain confident about our growth over the last quarter and our outlook for the holiday season, which is reflected in our guidance. However, we won’t discuss specific details regarding royalties.

title: Operator

speaker: Thomas J. Szkutak
title: CFO
content: Regarding the fulfillment centers, as I mentioned 90 days ago, we provided guidance for Q3's top line but not for Q4. We were optimistic about the growth in the first half of the year and wanted to see how Q3 performed. I previously stated that we planned to open 15 centers, possibly more, and we are now actually opening 17. This reflects our confidence not only in past growth but also in how it influences our future plans. We are optimistic about the growth we are experiencing and are considering various factors, including our recent historical growth rates. We are also seeing very strong pre-orders for the Kindle Fire and are increasing our capacity to produce millions more than initially planned. We are preparing for a fantastic holiday season for all our customers and especially for Kindle customers.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator

And then secondly, your shipping costs were also up pretty significantly, how much of that is Prime usage versus Prime customer acquisition cost?

speaker: Thomas J. Szkutak
title: CFO
content: In terms of employment, we are not providing guidance or estimates beyond the current quarter. However, we are experiencing a significant increase in employment both sequentially and year-over-year, especially in various areas. The most notable growth is in our operations and customer service associates, which constitute the majority of our new hires. We are also investing in other areas given our growth opportunities. Regarding the shift margin, Prime is having a considerable impact, along with our free shipping offers, and this is driving the situation.

title: Operator

title: CFO

We're very excited about it and think they're very interesting long-term opportunities. We are able to take advantage of our European infrastructure and leadership team to launch those two geographies, and we're very excited about it.

CSOI decreased 26% to $462 million, or 2.7% of revenue, down approximately 216 basis points year-over-year. Excluding the favorable impact from foreign exchange, CSOI decreased 27%. Unlike CSOI, our GAAP operating income includes stock-based compensation expense and other operating expense. GAAP operating income decreased 45% to $260 million, or 1.5% of net sales. Our income tax expense was $86 million in Q4, resulting in a 32% rate for the quarter and a 31% rate for the full year 2011. GAAP net income was $177 million, or $0.38 per diluted share, compared with $416 million and $0.91 per diluted share. Now I'll discuss the full year results. Revenue grew 41% to $48.08 billion. North America revenue grew 43% to $26.71 billion, and International grew 38% to $21.37 billion, 31% growth excluding year-over-year changes in foreign exchange rates. Consolidated Segment Operating Income, or CSOI, decreased 19% to $1.57 billion, or 21% excluding the favorable year-over-year impact from foreign exchange. And operating margin decreased 239 basis points to 3.3%. GAAP operating income decreased 39% to $862 million, or 1.8% of net sales. Turning to the balance sheet, cash and marketable securities increased $814 million year-over-year to $9.58 billion. Inventory increased 56% to $4.99 billion. And inventory turns were 10.3, down from 11.4 turns a year ago as we expanded selection, improved in-stock levels and introduced new product categories. Accounts payable increased 38% to $11.14 billion, and accounts payable days increased to 74 from 72 in the prior year. Our Q4 2011 capital expenditures were $550 million. The increase in capital expenditures reflects additional investments in support of continued business growth, including investments in technology, infrastructure, including Amazon Web Services and additional capacity to support our fulfillment operations. I'll conclude my portion of today's call with guidance. Incorporated into our guidance are the order trends that we've seen to date and what we believe today to be appropriately conservative assumptions. Our results are inherently unpredictable and may be materially affected by many factors, including a high level of uncertainty surrounding exchange rate fluctuations, as well as the global economy and consumer spending. It's not possible to accurately predict demand, and therefore, our actual results could differ materially from our guidance. As we described in more detail in our public filings, issues such as settling intercompany balances in foreign currencies amongst our subsidiaries, unfavorable resolution of legal matters and changes to our effective tax rates can all have a material effect on guidance. Our guidance further assumes that we don't conclude any additional business acquisitions or investments, record any further revisions to stock-based compensation estimates and that foreign exchange rates remain approximately where they've been recently. For Q1 2012, we expect net sales between $12 billion and $13.4 billion, a growth of between 22% and 36%. This guidance anticipates approximately 50 basis points of unfavorable impact from foreign exchange. GAAP operating income or loss to be between a loss of $200 million and $100 million of income, or between 162% decline and 69% decline. This includes approximately $200 million for stock-based compensation and amortization of intangible assets. We anticipate Consolidated Segment Operating Income, which excludes stock-based compensation and other operating expense, to be between 0 and $300 million, or between 100% decline and 36% decline. We remain heads-down focused on driving a better customer experience through price, selection and convenience. We believe putting customers first is the only reliable way to create lasting value for shareholders. Thanks. And with that, Sean, let's move to questions.

speaker: Sean Boyle
title: Vice President of Investor Relations
content: Great. Thanks, Tom. Let's move on to the Q&A portion of the call. Operator, will you please remind our listeners how to initiate a question?

title: Operator
content: And we'll take our first question from analyst Jeetil Patel from Deutsche Bank Securities.

speaker: Jeetil J. Patel
title: Analyst
content: A couple of questions, actually. First of all, on the Kindle Fire, I guess, Tom, can you maybe talk about Kindle Fire hardware units? Or did you see an increase in terms of unit sales on a month-on-month basis in terms of linearity? speaker: Thomas J. Szkutak
title: CFO
content: In terms of data related to Kindle Fire and actually Kindle itself, the only thing I can help you with is on the holiday season, which we put in the release. Our unit sales nearly tripled. It was up 177%, and that includes both our Kindle e-reader and Kindle Fire. So we're very pleased with the great growth we had. And obviously, we've been growing quite fast over the last several years from a unit perspective in launching Kindle. So it's on a very good base. In terms of fulfillment and delivery time, we're continually trying to improve all of our processes around from a customer standpoint, and that includes fulfillment and delivery speed. And so you've seen over the last several years, we've gotten closer and closer to customers from a delivery speed standpoint. And when we do that, it not only helps our retail offering, but it helps also our third parties who are participating in Fulfilled by Amazon. And one of the things that you're seeing in our Q4 numbers is we saw very good unit growth. And you're seeing that we expanded our third party as a percentage of total units. And one of the ways we did that is certainly by Fulfilled by Amazon because again, from a customer standpoint, those units are available for express 2-day shipping or 1-day if you're a Prime member and you pay the small fee, as well as our free shipping offers.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: And we'll take our next question from analyst Scott Devitt from Morgan Stanley.

speaker: Scott W. Devitt
title: Analyst
content: Two if I could. The first one, Tom, North American segment sales decelerated, and if you can, adjustment for Kindle Fire, by a pretty good bit. speaker: Thomas J. Szkutak
title: CFO
content: Sure. Regarding our overall performance, I will address the total global figures as well as the North American segment. Our growth rate for global revenue was 34%, not accounting for exchange rates, which is a decrease from 39% in Q3 and 37% the previous year. Our paid unit growth globally in Q4 was 46%, compared to 37% in Q4 last year, indicating an acceleration in unit growth. Additionally, third-party units experienced a year-over-year growth of 65%, accounting for 36% of total units, up from 32%. This reflects strong adoption, particularly from third-party sellers, and significant growth in Fulfillment by Amazon (FBA) over recent years, affecting our revenue figures. However, we only recognize a portion of the revenue based on the commissions we earn from that business. This trend is also evident in North America and internationally.  In North America, regarding our EGM revenue, some subcategories were impacted by the Thailand floods, which affected supply. The positive aspect is that we had strong third-party offerings in those subcategories. Furthermore, we observed robust growth in digital media sectors, including books, video, and music. However, in video games, which includes both consoles and games, we experienced a year-over-year revenue decline. This decline occurred despite strong third-party offerings and unit growth in video games, which impacted the North American media figures when comparing to Q4 last year. These dynamics illustrate that while third-party seller performance positively influences our operating income, we only report a portion of those sales, which affected our overall growth. This is why our operating income came in slightly above the initial guidance we provided.

speaker: Scott W. Devitt
title: Analyst
content: Regarding capital expenditures, if we look back to 2005, they were slightly above 2% of revenue and have been increasing since then. Although the last two years included costs for building, we concluded 2012 with capital expenditures at approximately 3.7% of revenue on a trailing basis. Could you discuss how we should approach capital expenditures as a percentage of revenue in the coming years?

speaker: Thomas J. Szkutak
title: CFO
content: We look at growth incrementally, considering both unit growth and the net present values of our specific investments. Breaking it down, we've seen significant growth in our retail offerings, our third-party sales through Fulfilled by Amazon, and AWS. The capacity required to support our operations and the infrastructure for our Web Services and Retail has been substantial. However, we believe we are effectively utilizing our capital. As mentioned in the last call, we planned to add 17 fulfillment centers in 2011, bringing our total to 69, which shows the high growth we are experiencing. We are very positive about the investments we are making, and with a 46% increase in paid units in Q4, we continue to see strong growth.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: Our next question is coming from analyst Mark Mahaney from the firm of Citi.

speaker: Mark S. Mahaney
title: Analyst
content: Tom, just a little more color on that North American media growth. You talked about the unit trends and the revenue trends in video games. Anything you'd want to call out in terms of the other media segments: books, music and video? And then real briefly, the share buybacks. I think this is the first time in at least 2 years you've done that. Any particular reason why you brought back stock in the quarter?

speaker: Thomas J. Szkutak
title: CFO
content: In North America, we are seeing very strong growth across all digital media. I also want to highlight that physical books experienced double-digit unit growth in Q4 year-over-year, which we found encouraging, especially considering the shift towards digital content and the rapid growth of the Kindle. Regarding video games, while revenue was down, third-party gross merchandise sales saw a strong increase, and total unit growth in video games was positive. However, there are challenging comparisons to consider, particularly with consoles. Video games, which includes both console and digital formats, tend to be very seasonal, with Q4 sales typically being significantly higher than in other quarters due to this seasonality. On the topic of stock purchases, there's not much to add; we have previously stated that we will buy shares opportunistically when we see appropriate value, and that is exactly what we did.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: Our next question is coming from analyst Spencer Wang from the firm of Crédit Suisse.

speaker: Spencer Wang
title: Analyst
content: Tom, 2 quick questions. One is, I think the new disclosure on service sales, maybe I missed the footnote in the press release, could you just clarify what's included there? Is that 3P, FBA, Prime, AWS and shipping? Or did I maybe miss something? And then secondly, can you share with us maybe your plans for how many fulfillment centers you plan on opening in 2012?

speaker: Thomas J. Szkutak
title: CFO
content: Sure. In terms of the disclosure, I would want to guide you right to the release to see exactly what's included in there. But certainly, in terms of some of the big pieces, it is our third-party. It is also AWS and a number of other service offerings. And so those are again documented well there, and I'd like to point you to that. Also, you can see that it's growing very well, and it reflects on the comments I made earlier about the fast-growing AWS businesses, the fast-growing third-party business. Service revenue is up approximately 74% year-over-year in Q4. And then in terms of fulfillment, we added 17 new FCs in 2011. That's globally. We do plan, based on the strong growth, to add more in 2012. As you can imagine, coming out of Q4, we're finalizing our plans for what we're going to do there. And you'll have to stay tuned, and we'll keep you updated as we go throughout the year.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: And our next question comes from Youssef Squali with Jefferies & Company.

speaker: Youssef H. Squali
title: Analyst
content: Can you help us understand the impact of video games revenue, specifically regarding the level of deceleration? We expected that with the launch of Kindle Fire, we would see a higher attach rate and consequently, stronger media revenue growth. Also, do you have any plans to offer separate pricing for the video streaming product? That's all.

speaker: Thomas J. Szkutak
title: CFO
content: Yes, to clarify, when discussing our growth rates, I'm referring to our digital content businesses which experienced significant growth in Q4. The video games, along with our physical and console businesses, showed strong seasonal performance. This is consistent with previous years, as the business is typically very seasonal and peaks in Q4. However, what is different this year is that revenue growth declined year-over-year, although unit sales increased due to strong third-party sales in Q4. It's important to note that consoles are part of this and they, along with video games, are included in our video games line within North America media. There have been several new offerings recently that have been highlighted in other press releases and updates.

speaker: Youssef H. Squali
title: Analyst
content: And on the video streaming?

speaker: Thomas J. Szkutak
title: CFO
content: I'm sorry, what was your question on that? Could you repeat it again?

speaker: Youssef H. Squali
title: Analyst
content: Are there any short-term plans to separate the video streaming service from Kindle and offer it as a standalone product?

speaker: Thomas J. Szkutak
title: CFO
content: For digital video, we have a few different options available. One is a paid or rental service through Amazon Video. Another is included with Prime. We appreciate both offerings and have mentioned their growth rates in our release. We are also pleased with the performance of Prime Video. While it's still early, we are enthusiastic about the progress we see. We are investing in digital content, and the adoption rates are promising. We are analyzing various metrics associated with this business, and again, it's still early, but we are satisfied with our observations so far. We will keep a close eye on it and continue to expand our content offerings.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: And our next question is coming from analyst Heather Bellini with firm Goldman Sachs.

speaker: Heather Bellini
title: Analyst
content: I was wondering if you could comment a little bit about any cannibalization you think you saw in traditional Kindle readers as a result of the Fire launch. And subsequently, how are you feeling about the Prime conversion of the Fire units versus your expectations?

speaker: Thomas J. Szkutak
title: CFO
content: Both devices, the readers and Fire, performed very well, and we are pleased with the growth we are experiencing. This growth is reflected in the growth rate we reported during the holiday season, which was up 177% year-over-year. Our Kindle reader business has been growing rapidly over the past several years since its introduction, which provides a solid foundation for this growth. Customers are enjoying both the reader and the Fire. It is still early to assess Prime conversion, but we are encouraged by the initial statistics we are observing. We will continue to monitor this closely and are optimistic about what we are seeing.

title: Operator

And certainly, you're seeing it also in our operating costs. And again, we're fortunate to have a lot of opportunities. We're fortunate to have the growth that we're experiencing, and that's why you're seeing that growth. But certainly, you'll see that. As you have over time, you'll see that growth rate will go in cycles. But we certainly are feeding the growth that we're seeing and the opportunities that we have.

This situation is affecting our overall growth rate, although it's hard to quantify the extent. Over the past couple of years, we have expanded into new markets, specifically Italy and Spain, and we are putting resources into those areas. Additionally, we continue to invest in China, which is growing rapidly and presents a promising long-term opportunity. These factors are influencing our International operations, and we are maintaining our investments in both regions. Regarding third-party growth, we are experiencing strong performance in International and North America, which we find encouraging. We are also investing on behalf of our customers and sellers, as well as for the retail capacity we require.

speaker: Scott W. Devitt
title: Analyst
content: And then secondly, on the employee base growth, I don't know if thinking about unit growth is the right way to think about it. But is there a point in time where you think the employee base starts to grow more in line possibly with unit growth? And can you maybe walk through where you're adding most significantly that's driving the headcount growth?

speaker: Thomas J. Szkutak
title: CFO
content: We are adding numerous resources across various areas. When you examine both year-over-year and sequentially, the Q1 figures you see are primarily in operations and customer service, which reflect the hiring we undertook following Q4. In Q4, we supplemented our workforce with temporary staff and have retained many of them post-Q4. To address your other question, we will certainly moderate this growth at some point. However, given the current growth we are experiencing, we are investing and ensuring we have the necessary resources to support that.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: And we'll take our next question from Mark Mahaney with Citi.

speaker: Mark S. Mahaney
title: Analyst
content: Tom, could you provide more details on the trends in gross margin? It seems that shipping costs have shown less deleverage for the first time in a while. Have you reached a tipping point there? Regarding gross margins, the significant increase over the last few quarters, is that mostly due to changes in product or revenue mix? Is there anything else contributing to that? Additionally, could you briefly discuss AmazonSupply.com? Has the inventory accumulated for its launch impacted inventory levels and turnover, or should we expect to see that effect in the future?

speaker: Thomas J. Szkutak
title: CFO
content: We're not providing specific gross margin figures. However, when examining the relationship between cost of goods sold and revenue, we are noticing several influencing factors. One significant factor is our business mix. Additionally, as I mentioned earlier, growth from third parties has also played a role. This quarter, we experienced substantial unit growth, which was an improvement from the previous quarter, showing sequential growth. Third-party units made up a larger share of total units, increasing by approximately 300 basis points compared to last year, with third-party unit growth exceeding 60% again in Q1. These elements are affecting our operating margins. Regarding AmazonSupply.com, we have enough inventory to support that business and are optimistic about its long-term potential. The inventory increase we are seeing is widespread across various businesses, categories, and geographical areas, which is driving this change.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: And we'll take our next question from Heather Bellini with Goldman Sachs.

speaker: Heather Bellini
title: Analyst
content: I had 2 for you. First, I was wondering if you could talk about just over the last few years if you could give us a sense how much of the third-party increase has been related to agency e-books. And then the second question is in light of the DOJ case, I was wondering if you could walk us through your thoughts about the agency e-book model, as well as whether or not this will mean we should see things move back to wholesale.

speaker: Thomas J. Szkutak
title: CFO
content: Yes, I can't provide much help regarding your questions. We believe the lawsuit is a significant win for Kindle owners, and we look forward to having the ability to reduce prices on more Kindle books. The growth in our paid units, not including third-party sales, has certainly been bolstered by e-books. Their growth has been rapid, positively affecting the growth rate you've observed over the past few years, which has been beneficial for us and our customers. Beyond that, I don’t have much more to add.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: And we'll go next to Ken Sena with Evercore Partners.

speaker: Kenneth Sena
title: Analyst
content: In your press release, you mentioned the launch of your Amazon Appstore. And can you just share any thoughts on current traction on Android or specifically off Kindle Fire? And what are some of the advantages and disadvantages that you see for Amazon in that area?

speaker: Thomas J. Szkutak
title: CFO
content: It's early, so there's not a lot I can do. We're excited about it. We think it's a very interesting opportunity and happy to do that on behalf of our customers. But stay tuned, and it's early.

speaker: Kenneth Sena
title: Analyst
content: And maybe one more follow-up. If you can just maybe talk about any of the traction you're seeing within Kindle Fire more broadly or any thoughts you have maybe around Kindle smartphone, that'd be great, too.

speaker: Thomas J. Szkutak
title: CFO
content: In terms of the Kindle Fire, we are pleased with the growth that we're seeing and customers are buying a lot of content. And you're seeing that when you look at particularly in North America. When you look at our North American media growth from Q4 to Q1, you're seeing that accelerate. And that's certainly a big part of it. And so we're very pleased with what's happening, and we're going to continue to add more and more content for customers and across all of our digital categories. And we think we have a great value proposition for customers today, and we're going to continue to make that better over time.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: And we'll take our next question from Doug Anmuth with JP Morgan.

speaker: Douglas Anmuth
title: Analyst
content: I want to ask 2 things, Tom. If you could first just give us some more color on the outlook around segment operating income in 2Q and just how we should be thinking about the drivers there in terms of the sequential decline. And then secondly, just the North American media business, you saw good reacceleration from 4Q to 1Q. Can you talk about the factors there leading to that acceleration?

speaker: Thomas J. Szkutak
title: CFO
content: Sure. I'll take the second one first on North American media. I just mentioned that a little bit in one of the previous questions. But certainly, our digital media growth has been great and certainly it's helping that. One other call-out, just to keep in mind, in Q4, I had mentioned that video games, including video game consoles, the consoles are part of North America media, that's a seasonal business that was bringing down growth in Q4. So it's also something to keep in mind. In terms of our guidance, we've given a pretty broad range on both the top and the bottom as we have previously. We think the segment operating income on the bottom end of the range is certainly appropriately conservative. But again, things that you should think about, we'll continue to add capacity as we've talked about in the past. With the growth that we're experiencing, we are adding more. And as I mentioned on one of the earlier questions, we've announced approximately 13 new fulfillment centers. So those are as a result of the growth that we're experiencing. We're also adding capacity to support AWS in our retail business on the infrastructure side as well. So those are things to think about as you think about Q2 from a segment operating income, as well as the CapEx that I mentioned in the opening. Another area is certainly our digital offerings. We are certainly adding more content, and specifically, more video content, which will be as reflected in our guidance. And so those are factors, among others, that you should think about.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: And we'll take our next question from Gene Munster with Piper Jaffray.

speaker: Charles Eugene Munster
title: Analyst
content: Another question on gross margin. It was obviously impressive results, the best in 3 years almost. And it's been a little bit of a roller coaster in terms of the profitability quarter-to-quarter. And we understand that you're in an investment phase and there's a massive opportunity ahead of you. Is there anything that you can tell us as we think going forward over the next few quarters? Just is the investment philosophy that played through this quarter going to play on in other quarters? Or is each quarter kind of its own 3 months and it could go either way?

speaker: Thomas J. Szkutak
title: CFO
content: Yes. Gene, regarding guidance, we are only providing guidance for Q2 at this time. However, I want to emphasize that we are experiencing strong growth, as evidenced in Q1 and reflected in our Q2 guidance. We will need to wait and see how the rest of the year unfolds as we move forward. We are very optimistic about the opportunities we have. We believe we are in an excellent position with these opportunities. Although we have achieved some scale, we still see tremendous potential ahead, which is why we are making investments in these areas.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: And we'll go next to Brian Nowak with Nomura.

speaker: Brian Nowak
title: Analyst
content: I have a couple of questions. The first one is I know there's a lot of focus on kind of CSOI margins and margin pressure from the build. But I was just curious if you still see areas of your business in the oldest part of your business, where you think you have inefficiencies you can still work to improve execution and kind of get some margin lift out of those in the oldest part of the business just to improve execution. And the second one is any more clarity on how much roughly Quidsi and Lovefilm added to revenue growth this quarter?

speaker: Thomas J. Szkutak
title: CFO
content: In terms of opportunities for improvement, we have made significant progress, but we still recognize there is much more we can enhance across our business. The greatest potential lies in the newer segments. However, we also continue to strive for improved productivity and are implementing programs to achieve that in all of our operations. There are numerous areas to cover, but we focus on productivity across all aspects of our business. We see opportunities to collaborate with vendors more effectively to secure better savings and pricing for our customers. While the list of opportunities is extensive, we believe that the ranking of these opportunities, especially in terms of basis points improvement, starts with the newer initiatives we have launched and generally leads back to where the largest potential for improvement exists in terms of basis points.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: And we'll take our next question from Matt Nemer with Wells Fargo Securities.

speaker: Matthew R. Nemer
title: Analyst
content: Just going back to the gross margin, is it fair to say, given the change in that metric and the change in third-party units, that potentially the core margins in 1P really accelerated in the first quarter in addition to there being a continued mix shift to 3P? That's my first question. And then secondly, can you comment on any product categories in either media or EGM that either held you back in the quarter or were a tailwind? I think last quarter you mentioned video games and a few categories in terms of giving some color.

speaker: Thomas J. Szkutak
title: CFO
content: Yes. Regarding the second part of your question about headwinds, I would say there are a few areas, as discussed last quarter, related to the supply issues from the Thailand floods. These caused challenges particularly in the areas of cameras, audio, video, and office equipment. You saw some impact from this in Q4, as well as in Q1. The good news for us is that our platform consists of many different sellers. So for items we had in supply, we were able to offer those to customers. In cases where we didn't have inventory, we often found third-party sellers that still had stock available. This greatly assisted us in navigating that situation. Those are some of the headwinds we faced in Q1. On the positive side, we experienced strong growth across many retail categories, particularly in Kindle. Globally, AWS continues to grow very quickly, providing us with significant favorable tailwinds from this strong growth.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: We'll take our next question from Carlos Kirjner with Sanford Bernstein.

speaker: Carlos Kirjner
title: Analyst
content: Two questions, if I may. First, on fulfillment. If you think of the expected authorization of your fulfillment network in the fourth quarter of this year versus what you had in the fourth quarter of '11, do you expect it to be the same, higher or lower? And secondly, on Kindle, now that you are a manufacturer, a seller of Android-based devices, can you comment on your intellectual property position and the strategic and financial risks associated with potential lawsuits from competitors? For example, do you intend to go buy patents in the market?

speaker: Thomas J. Szkutak
title: CFO
content: Regarding the first question about fulfillment utilization, it's tough to determine what our utilization will be at this moment. We have a dedicated team in each of our locations working to ensure we maintain adequate capacity throughout the year, including Q4. It's always a challenging balance; we need enough capacity to meet customer demands. As the year progresses, we'll see how growth develops. Based on our current experience, we expect solid growth, but we’ll need to monitor the situation in the coming months and quarters. It’s still early to predict our utilization levels, but our goal is to have sufficient capacity without excess, which is a delicate balance that makes predictions difficult. As for your second question, I can't provide much more information on that. We have a lot of proprietary technology and a strong technical team exploring various interesting areas for our customers, and we'll continue to do so. Beyond that, I don't have much else to add.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: And we'll go next to Jordan Rohan with Stifel, Nicolaus.

speaker: Jordan Rohan
title: Analyst
content: A couple of point of clarification. I don't think I heard you blame macro weakness in Europe. Now clearly, you had stronger results across-the-board, so I don't see it evident in the results. Are you clear enough about the direction of the macro or its impact on your European operations that you can kind of say, at least from what you're seeing, it's not affecting you now? And the second question is on this percentage of third-party versus first-party sales. Last quarter, I believe you said that it got up to 36% in part because of stockouts due to the Thai flood and such. At some point, one would think that the supply chain for cameras and other equipment affected by the Thai flood would normalize. Would we expect that to therefore normalize back down from 39% level back down to the mid-30s? How can we think about that relationship?

speaker: Thomas J. Szkutak
title: CFO
content: Sure. Regarding the macroeconomic situation in Europe, we aren't exactly a key indicator for the economy, making it difficult to evaluate the overall impact. It is certainly affecting us, and you are likely familiar with the current challenges based on what you've been reading. However, quantifying that impact remains complicated.  For third-party sales, we have noticed that the dynamics you mentioned have indeed assisted us with stockouts in both the fourth quarter and the first quarter, which has contributed to our growth. It’s hard to predict where that will stabilize, but outside these two quarters, we have experienced significant growth in third-party sales, which has been accelerating over the past couple of years.  Several factors contribute to improving the experience for sellers, with the most significant being Fulfilled by Amazon. This change positively affects all the regions where we operate. It’s beneficial for sellers, customers, and shareholders, creating a promising intersection. We’re very enthusiastic about this progress, which is the main driving force behind it. Stockouts will occur occasionally in various categories, but I don't consider that the primary reason for the growth in third-party sales over the past few years. Rather, it's the various improvements we've implemented to enhance sellers' experiences.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: And we'll go next to Lloyd Walmsley with Deutsche Bank.

speaker: Lloyd Walmsley
title: Analyst
content: Just had a couple questions around AmazonSupply. And I guess, first, wondering if this is the beginning of a bigger push into the B2B kind of industrial space. And then secondly, what do you all see as your strongest assets as you approach this space? Are you planning to rely a lot on third party for inventory? And then just finally, along those lines, the press release mentions the extension of corporate credit. Wondering how integral this might be to the strategy. And then just more broadly, how do you think about credit extension to customers?

speaker: Thomas J. Szkutak
title: CFO
content: Regarding AmazonSupply, we have been supporting businesses for quite some time. This new URL aims to enhance that support with a compelling selection for businesses. Our collaboration with numerous businesses is strong, both as customers on the consumer side and through various third-party sellers in our seller business. We are enthusiastic about this initiative. As for credit extension and related matters, we are actively working on those aspects and aim to make well-considered decisions for our customers. While I can't provide much more information at this moment, we would be happy to discuss it further as things develop.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: And we'll go next to Anthony DiClemente with Barclays.

speaker: Anthony DiClemente
title: Analyst
content: On the Kiva acquisition, I was wondering if you could talk about how you're planning on implementing that at your fulfillment centers. And does it require much incremental investment? And then more broadly about mobile purchasing behavior, wondering if you could speak to just the purchasing behavior you're seeing from your consumers in terms of what's the order of magnitude and what type of mix shift in buying that you're seeing from PC and mobile? That would be great.

speaker: Thomas J. Szkutak
title: CFO
content: In terms of Kiva, it's early. We haven't closed it yet. And so we're very, very excited to be having Kiva and the team as part of the Amazon team. We're extremely excited to have that. And in terms of implementations within Amazon, we still have a lot of work to do to figure out how and when we'll do that. And so those are things that we'll be working on. But we're very, very excited about the opportunity to join with Kiva. So we're excited about it. In terms of mobile, not a lot I can help you with there. Certainly, the mobile part of our business is growing very, very fast. And it's a very exciting opportunity. And this is not something that's new; it's something that we've been working on for a number of years in a number of geographies. And we'll continue to work on that experience to make it even better for customers over time.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: And we'll go next to Justin Post with Bank of America Merrill Lynch.

speaker: A. Justin Post
title: Analyst
content: First question is on taxes. Can you help us at all understand what percent of your marketplaces currently pay taxes similar to, say, offline retail? And maybe any help on what you saw on New York with the tax law changes there. Maybe start with that, and then one follow-up.

speaker: Thomas J. Szkutak
title: CFO
content: I'm sorry. Could you repeat the first part of the question?

speaker: A. Justin Post
title: Analyst
content: Yes. What percent of your market, including International markets, are already on what we call level-tax basis, meaning the taxes are the same for buying on Amazon versus an offline retailer?

speaker: Thomas J. Szkutak
title: CFO
content: Yes. So you're saying sales tax. Assume that approximately 50% of our sales, we either collect a sales tax or a value-added tax. So we collect it in several states today in the U.S. and a large number of geographies outside of the U.S. And so it's approximately 50%. So this is not anything new. This is something that we've been doing for a long period of time. And we have very good businesses in those geographies and states that we collect.

speaker: A. Justin Post
title: Analyst
content: And did you see any slowdown in states where they've enacted sales taxes in your sales levels?

speaker: Thomas J. Szkutak
title: CFO
content: Yes. I can't comment on any specific geography or state. But again, you can see by the growth that we've experienced over the past few years, which includes during those past few years, certainly adding some geographies, if you will, to our collection efforts. And so those are all represented in the results that you've seen over the past few years and several years. So that's all I can add to that.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: And we'll go next to Herman Leung with Susquehanna Financial Group.

speaker: Herman Leung
title: Analyst
content: I have two quick questions. First, I know there's significant investment happening in the data center area for your Web Services business. I'm curious about the current capacity you are able to support, especially as you take on more larger customers on the government side. I have a quick follow-up.

speaker: Thomas J. Szkutak
title: CFO
content: Yes. No, we're ready for additional demand. The team has worked extremely hard to make sure that we keep up with demand. And so as you've seen over the past few years now, you're seeing our CapEx growing. As a result of it, you're seeing the operating expense as it relates to that in our technology and content. And so the team has done a very nice job in terms of adding capacity and is very excited to continue this fast growth that we're experiencing in AWS. So we're very happy to do that.

speaker: Herman Leung
title: Analyst
content: I have a quick follow-up regarding the GMV from your third-party business. Is there a chance that in the future you could share more about the actual third-party volume contributing to the top line?

speaker: Thomas J. Szkutak
title: CFO
content: The best way to think about our retail and third-party business is that it’s not a direct comparison due to the presence of both new and used products, as well as a different mix of categories. However, from a volume perspective, it accounted for approximately 39% of our total units, which is quite significant and has grown over 60% this quarter compared to 36% last quarter. While I can’t provide the gross merchandise value, it's important to note that 39% of our total units come from our retail units, making it substantial.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: And we'll go next to Ben Schachter with Macquarie.

speaker: Benjamin A. Schachter
title: Analyst
content: Given the success of the ad-supported Kindle, should we expect more devices to be offered with an ad-supported option? And then also if any comments on the dynamics driving the increase in the shipping revenue. And finally, any update on the share buyback?

speaker: Thomas J. Szkutak
title: CFO
content: Yes. In terms of what we do going forward, we certainly have a long-standing practice of not talking about what we would do going forward, so you have to stay tuned on that. In terms of the share repurchase, as I mentioned in the opening comments, we purchased 5.3 million shares, just under $1 billion, $960 million during the quarter. We have a little over $700 million or just under $800 million left on our authorization that we have from the board, which was $2 billion, that we got some ago. So that's left on the authorization.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: And we'll take our last question from Colin Sebastian with R.W. Baird.

speaker: Gregor Schauer
title: Analyst
content: This is Gregor Schauer in for Colin. I have a question regarding the Kindle Fire, which you guys have noted for the quarter is still the #1 bestselling and most gifted product on Amazon.com. But it's still only selling in the U.S. Can you help us think through or understand sort of what are the other considerations in terms of the timing of an international rollout of the Kindle Fire?

speaker: Thomas J. Szkutak
title: CFO
content: I really can't. I think you'd have to stay tuned. It's certainly a very interesting opportunity for us. And we know that, and you'll have to stay tuned.

title: Operator
content: And that concludes our question-and-answer session. I'd like to turn the conference back to our speakers for any closing remarks.

speaker: Thomas J. Szkutak
title: CFO
content: Thank you for joining us on the call today and for your questions. A replay will be available on our Investor Relations website at least through the end of the quarter. We appreciate your interest in Amazon.com and look forward to talking with you again next quarter.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: Thank you, everyone. That does conclude today's conference. We thank you for your participation.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: Good day, everyone, and welcome to the Amazon.com Second Quarter 2012 Financial Results Teleconference. Today's call is being recorded. For opening remarks, I will be turning the call over to the Vice President of Investor Relations, Mr. Sean Boyle. Please go ahead.

speaker: Sean Boyle
title: Vice President of Investor Relations
content: Hello, and welcome to our Q2 2012 financial results conference call. Joining us today is Tom Szkutak, our CFO. We will be available for questions after our prepared remarks. The following discussion and responses to your questions reflect management's views as of today, April 26, 2012, only and will include forward-looking statements. Actual results may differ materially. Additional information about factors that could potentially impact our financial results is included in today's press release and our filings with the SEC, including our most recent Annual Report on Form 10-K. As you listen to today's conference call, we encourage you to have our press release in front of you, which includes our financial results, as well as metrics and commentary on the quarter. During this call, we will discuss certain non-GAAP financial measures. In our press release, slides accompanying this webcast and our filings with the SEC, each of which is posted on our IR website, you'll find additional disclosures regarding these non-GAAP measures, including reconciliations of these measures with comparable GAAP measures. Finally, unless otherwise stated, all comparisons in this call will be against our results for the comparable period of 2011. Now I'll turn the call over to Tom.

speaker: Tom Szkutak
title: CFO
content: Thanks, Sean. I will begin with comments on our second quarter financial results. Trailing 12 months operating cash flow was $3.22 billion compared with $3.2 billion. Trailing 12-month free cash flow decreased 40% to $1.1 billion. Return on invested capital was 11%, down from 21%. ROIC is trailing 12-month free cash flow divided by average total assets minus current liabilities excluding the current portion of long-term debt over five quarter ends. The combination of common stock, stock-based awards outstanding, was 468 million shares compared with 468 million shares. Worldwide revenue grew 29% to $12.83 billion or 32% excluding the $272 million unfavorable impact from the year-over-year changes in foreign exchange rates. We are grateful to our customers who continue to take advantage of our low prices, vast selection and shipping offers. Media revenue increased to $4.12 billion, up 13% or 15% excluding foreign exchange. EGM revenue increased to $8.16 billion, up 38% or 42% excluding foreign exchange. Worldwide EGM increased to 64% of worldwide sales, up from 59%. Worldwide paid unit growth was 43%. Active customer counts exceeded 180 million. Worldwide active seller accounts were more than 2 million. Seller units were 40% of paid units compared to 36% of paid units in Q2 of 2011. Now I will discuss operating expenses excluding stock-based compensation. Cost of sales was $9.49 billion, or 73.9% of revenue compared with 75.9%. Fulfillment, marketing, technology and content and G&A combined, was $2.99 billion or 23.3% of sales, up approximately 307 basis points year-over-year. Fulfillment was $1.3 billion or 10.1% of revenue compared with 9.2%. Tech and content was $970 million or 7.6% of revenue compared with 6.3%. Marketing was $521 million or 4.1% of revenue compared with 3.3%. Now I will talk about our segment results and, consistent with prior periods, we do not allocate to segments our stock-based compensation or other operating expense line item. In the North America segment, revenue grew 36% to $7.33 billion. Media revenue grew 18% to $1.87 billion, EGM revenue grew 41% to $4.94 billion representing 67% of North America revenues, up from 65%. North America segment operating income increased 61% to $344 million a 4.7% operating margin. In the international segment, revenue grew 22% to $5.51 billion adjusting for the $269 million year-over-year unfavorable foreign exchange impact, revenue growth was 28%. Media revenue grew 8% to $2.25 billion or 12% excluding foreign exchange. EGM revenue grew 34% to $3.22 billion or 42% excluding foreign exchange. EGM now represents 59% of international revenues, up from 53%. International segment operating income decreased 91% to $16 million or 0.3% operating margin. Excluding the unfavorable impact from foreign exchange, international segment operating income decreased 74%. Consolidated segment operating income decreased 7% to $360 million or 2.8% of revenue, down approximately 109 basis points year-over-year. Excluding the unfavorable impact from foreign exchange, CSOI decreased 4%. Unlike CSOI, our GAAP operating income includes stock-based compensation expense and other operating expenses. GAAP operating income decreased 47% to $107 million or 0.8% of net sales. Our income tax expense was $109 million, a 75% effective tax rate for the quarter and includes a one-time expense of $51 million related to the integration of Kiva Systems acquisition. Accordingly, our Q2 2012 effective tax rate is higher than both our current estimated 2012 annual effective rate and our 2011 effective tax rate. GAAP net income was $7 million or $0.01 per diluted share compared with $191 million and $0.41 per diluted share. Q2 2012 net income includes $65 million of estimated loss related to the acquisition and integration of Kiva Systems. Turning to the balance sheet. Cash and marketable securities decreased $1.39 billion year-over-year to $4.97 billion. Inventory increased 36% to $4.3 billion and inventory turns were 10.1, down from 11.3 turns a year ago as we expanded selection, improved in-stock levels and introduced new product categories. Accounts payable increased 24% to $7.07 billion and accounts payable days decreased to 68 from 69 in the prior year. Our Q2 2012 capital expenditures were $657 million, the increase in capital expenditures reflects additional investments in support of continued business growth consisting of investments in technology infrastructure, including Amazon Web Services and additional capacity to support our funding operations. I’ll conclude my portion of today’s call with guidance. Incorporated into our guidance are the order trends that we have seen to date and what we believe today to be properly conservative assumptions. Our results are inherently unpredictable and may be materially affected by many factors including a high level of uncertainties surrounding exchange rate fluctuations as well as the global economy and consumer spending. It's not possible to accurately predict demand and therefore, our actual results could differ materially from our guidance. As we describe in more detail in our public filings, issues such as settling intercompany balances and foreign currencies among such subsidiaries, unfavorable resolution of legal matters, and changes to our effective tax rate can all have a material effect on guidance. Our guidance further assumes that we don’t conclude any additional business acquisitions, investments or settlements, record further revisions for stock-based compensation estimates, and that foreign exchange rates remain approximately where they have been recently. For Q3 2012, we expect net sales of between $12.9 billion and $14.3 billion or growth between 19% and 31%. This guidance anticipates approximately 425 basis points of unfavorable impact from foreign exchange rates. GAAP operating income or loss is expected to be between $350 million loss and $50 million loss, down from $79 million income in the comparable prior year period. This includes approximately $275 million for stock-based compensation and amortization of intangible assets. We anticipate consolidated segment operating income or loss, which excludes stock-based compensation and other operating expenses, to be between $75 million loss and $225 million in income, or between a 129% decline and a 14% decline. We expect capital expenditures, including capitalized software development, to be approximately $0.8 billion to $0.9 billion. These anticipated investments are driven primarily by our expectations of continued business growth consisting of investments in technology infrastructure, including Amazon Web Services and additional capacity to support our fulfillment operations. We remain focused on driving better customer experience through price, selection, and convenience. We believe putting customers first is the only reliable way to create lasting value for shareholders. Thanks. With that, Sean, we will move to questions.

speaker: Sean Boyle
title: Vice President of Investor Relations
content: Great. Thanks, Tom. Let's move on to the Q&A portion of the call. Operator, will you please remind our listeners how to initiate a question.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: (Operator Instructions) We will take our first question from Spencer Wang with Crédit Suisse.

speaker: Spencer Wang
title: Analyst
content: Thanks, good afternoon. Just one question on Kiva and a couple of parts, Tom. Now that you have closed the acquisition, can you talk about how you will deploy the Kiva technology? Is that for new fulfillment centers only or can you use that in your legacy fulfillment centers and perhaps what type of efficiencies that could gain? And then last part would be, is there any impact on your Q3 guidance from the Kiva acquisition specifically? Thanks.

speaker: Tom Szkutak
title: CFO
content: Sure. In terms of Kiva itself, we are very excited to have Kiva as part of the Amazon team. You know we are looking forward to getting great productivity over time through its use. But again it’s very early and you'll just have to stay tuned in terms of the plan. In terms of the impact, you mentioned Q3. Let me just provide a little bit of data on both Q2 actuals and Q3. In terms of GAAP operating income in Q2, it was negative $25 million. For Q3 it’s approximately negative $35 million. And then on the net income for Q2, it was a loss of approximately $65 million. And so those are the numbers for Q2 and Q3. But again we are very happy to have them on board and look forward to working with them going forward.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: We will go next to Heather Bellini with Goldman Sachs.

speaker: Heather Bellini
title: Analyst
content: Question on the gross margin, continues to climb up, and I was wondering if you could give any commentary there around how agency versus wholesale and eBooks is contributing to that?

speaker: Tom Szkutak
title: CFO
content: Yeah, the bigger issue is not that; it’s related to overall third-party sales. A number of factors are certainly driving the improvement in product gross margins that you are referring to. But as it relates to third-party sales, it’s on the broader third-party sales. So if you take a look from a units perspective, third-party was 40% of our total units in Q2. That’s up from 36%. So it’s approximately a 400 basis points increase as a percentage of total units, which is certainly one of the factors that you are seeing there.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: We will go next to Herman Leung with Susquehanna.

speaker: Unidentified Analyst
title: Analyst
content: This is Deepak sitting in for Herman. So the question I had was on the hardware business. So how important do you think is the hardware strategy to you for the digital content? Now given that Kindle Fire has been out there for a while, could you discuss the strategy on the business and how it’s driving the digital content?

speaker: Tom Szkutak
title: CFO
content: Sure. You know we are very excited about both the hardware and the content of the business. We think if you take a look at our devices, certainly it’s very integrated, which is great for customers. So we think it’s an incredible experience. And so we have been very excited about the progress we have made so far from both a device and content standpoint. And we are super excited about the roadmap that we have. So again, that’s, again, we are very happy with what the team is doing there.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: And we will go next to Brian Nowak with Nomura Equity Research.

speaker: Aram Rubinson
title: Analyst
content: This is Aram Rubinson sitting in for Brian Nowak. I notice your shipping cost was lower as a percent of sales for the first time in nearly three years. The driver looks like it's shipping cost per unit, which fell about 10%. Can you talk about how much of that might be attributable to the proximity of distribution centers to metro areas, lower fuel, more favorable carrier pricing etc., and whether or not you see anything on the horizon that would change that course?

speaker: Tom Szkutak
title: CFO
