speaker: Sean Boyle
title: Vice President of Investor Relations
content: Okay. Thank you for joining us on the call today and for your questions. A replay will be available on the investor relations website at least through the end of the quarter. We appreciate your interest in Amazon.com and look forward to talking with you again next quarter.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: Good day everyone, thank you for standing by. Welcome to the Amazon.com First Quarter 2013 Financial Results Teleconference. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. After the presentation, we will conduct a question-and-answer session. Today's call is being recorded. For opening remarks, I will be turning the call over to the Vice President of Investor Relations, Mr. Sean Boyle. Mr. Boyle, please go ahead.

speaker: Sean Boyle
title: Vice President of Investor Relations
content: Hello and welcome to our Q1 2013 financial results conference call. Joining us today is Tom Szkutak, our CFO. We will be available for questions after our prepared remarks. The following discussion and responses to your questions reflect management's views as of today, April 25, 2013 only and will include forward-looking statements. Actual results may differ materially. Additional information about factors that could potentially impact our financial results is included in today's press release and our filings with the SEC, including our most recent annual report on Form 10-K. As you listen to today's conference call, we encourage you to have our press release in front of you, which includes our financial results, as well as metrics and commentary on the quarter. During this call, we will discuss certain non-GAAP financial measures. In our press release, slides accompanying this webcast and our filings with the SEC, each of which is posted on our IR website, you will find additional disclosures regarding these non-GAAP measures, including reconciliations of these measures with comparable GAAP measures. Finally, unless otherwise stated, all comparisons in this call will be against our results for the comparable period of 2012. Now, I’ll turn the call over to Tom.

speaker: Tom Szkutak
title: CFO
content: Thanks Sean. I’ll begin with comments on our first quarter financial results. Trailing 12-month operating cash flow increased 39% to $4.25 billion. Trailing 12-month free cash flow decreased 85% to $177 million. Trailing-12 month capital expenditures were $4.07 billion. This amount includes $1.4 billion in purchases of our previously leased corporate office space, as well as property for the development of additional corporate office space located in Seattle, Washington, which we purchased in the fourth quarter of 2012. The increase in capital expenditures reflects additional investments in support of continued business growth consisting of investments in technology, infrastructure including Amazon Web Services, and additional capacity to support our fulfillment operations. Return on invested capital was 1%, down from 12%. ROIC is TTM free cash flow divided by average total assets minus current liabilities excluding the current portion of long-term debt over five quarter ends. The combination of common stock and stock-based awards outstanding was 471 million shares compared with 464 million one year ago. Worldwide revenue grew 22% to $16.07 billion or 24% excluding the $302 million unfavorable impact from year-over-year changes in foreign exchange rates. We are grateful to our customers who continue to take advantage of our low prices, vast selection, and shipping offers. Media revenue increased to $5.06 billion, up 7% or 10% excluding foreign exchange. EGM revenue increased to $10.21 billion, up 28% or 30% excluding foreign exchange. Worldwide EGM increased to 64% of worldwide sales, up from 60%. Worldwide paid unit growth was 30%. Active customer accounts exceeded 209 million. Worldwide active seller accounts were more than 2 million. Seller units represented 40% of paid units. Now, I will discuss operating expenses excluding stock-based compensation. Cost of sales was $11.8 billion, or 73.4% of revenue, compared with 76.1%. Fulfillment, marketing, technology and content and G&A combined was $3.83 billion, or 23.8% of sales, up approximately 289 basis points year-over-year. Fulfillment was $1.74 billion, or 10.8% of revenue compared with 9.5%. Tech and content was $1.26 billion, or 7.9% of revenue, compared with 6.5%. Marketing was $616 million, or 3.8% of revenue compared with 3.6%. Now, let’s talk about our segment results and consistent with prior periods, we do not allocate the segments, our stock-based compensation or other operating expense line items. In the North America segment, revenue grew 26% to $9.39 billion. Media revenue grew 14% to $2.51 billion. EGM revenue grew 28% to $6.13 billion, representing 65% of North America revenues, up from 64%. North America segment operating income increased 31% to $457 million, a 4.9% operating margin. In the international segment, revenue grew 16% to $6.68 billion. Adjusting for the $301 million year-over-year unfavorable foreign exchange impact, revenue growth was 21%. Media revenue grew 1% to $2.54 billion, or 7% excluding foreign exchange and EGM revenue grew 28% to $4.09 billion, or 32% excluding foreign exchange. EGM now represents 61% of international revenues, up from 56%. International segment operating loss was $16 million, a 0.2% negative operating margin compared with income of $49 million. CSOI increased 11% to $441 million, or 2.7% of revenue, down approximately 27 basis points year-over-year. Unlike CSOI, our GAAP operating income includes stock-based compensation expense and other operating expenses. GAAP operating income decreased 6% to $181 million, or 1.1% of net sales. Our income tax benefit was $18 million it includes $46 million of discrete tax benefits primarily resulting from the retroactive reinstatement of the federal research and development credit that was enacted in January 2013. GAAP net income was $82 million or $0.18 per diluted share compared with $130 million and $0.28 per diluted share. Turning to the balance sheet, cash and marketable securities increased $2.18 billion year over year to $7.89 billion. Inventory increased 27% to $5.4 billion and inventory turns were 9.5, down from 10.4 turns a year ago as we expanded selection, improved stock levels and introduced new product categories. Accounts payable increased 29% to $8.92 billion and accounts payable days increased to 68 from 62 in the prior year. I will conclude my portion of today’s call with guidance. Incorporated into our guidance are the order trends that we’ve seen to date and what we believe today to be appropriately conservative assumptions. Our results are inherently unpredictable and may be materially affected by many factors, including a high level of uncertainty surrounding exchange rate fluctuations as well as the global economy and consumer spending. It's not possible to accurately predict demand and therefore our actual results could differ materially from our guidance, as we’ve described in more detail in our public filings issues such as settling intercompany balances in foreign currencies among such subsidiaries, unfavorable resolution of legal matters, and changes to our effective tax rates can all have a material effect on guidance. Our guidance further assumes that we don't conclude any additional business acquisitions, investments or settlements, record any further revisions to stock-based compensation estimates and that foreign exchange rates remain approximately where they have been recently. For Q2 2013, we expect net sales of between $14.5 billion and $16.2 billion, a growth of between 13% and 26%. This guidance anticipates approximately 275 basis points of unfavorable impact on foreign exchange rates. GAAP operating income or loss to be between a $340 million loss and $10 million income compared to $107 million income in the prior year period. This includes approximately $340 million for stock-based compensation and amortization of intangible assets. We anticipate consolidated segment operating income, which excludes stock-based compensation and other operating expenses, to be between zero and $350 million compared to $360 million in the prior year period. We remain focused on driving a better customer experience through price, selection, and convenience. We believe putting customers first is the only reliable way to create lasting value for shareholders. Thanks. With that, Sean, let's move to questions.

speaker: Sean Boyle
title: Vice President of Investor Relations
content: Great. Thanks Tom. Let's move on to the Q&A portion of the call. Operator, will you please remind our listeners how to initiate a question?

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: Certainly. (Operator Instructions) And our first question today will come from analyst Brian Pitz with Jefferies.

speaker: Brian Pitz
title: Analyst
content: In February, you changed your FBA fulfillment fees. Any comments on how this affected third-party sales and what was the overall merchant response? And then just quickly any update on your latest plans for new fulfillment centers in 2013?

speaker: Tom Szkutak
title: CFO
content: I will address the second part of your question first. We have announced three new fulfillment centers in the U.S. and several outside the U.S., similar to last year. It’s still early, and we are very pleased with the growth we are seeing. We plan to add more fulfillment centers throughout the year, and we will keep you updated as we progress. Regarding FBA, there isn’t much I can share at this moment. However, we are very happy with the FBA business, and we believe it benefits both sellers and customers. We are glad to provide that service.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: Moving on, we will hear from Scott Devitt of Morgan Stanley.

speaker: Scott Devitt
title: Analyst
content: Tom, the international segment sales growth of 21% continues to show modest deceleration I think with the exception of 4Q, it’s been trailing U.S. growth. I understand that AWS is mostly booked in the U.S. so that’s a piece of the delta. But you’ve talked in the past quarters about the investments in international driving margin to at least breakeven levels in international. I wonder if you could just talk through deceleration in the revenue growth in those markets and whether that’s comp related, Europe macro or otherwise? And then secondly, shipping cost on a net basis is again leveraging. I think that’s a second consecutive quarter. I just wonder if you could refresh us in terms of when the accounting change occurred in terms of the shipping revenue calculation for FPA to just understand if that’s an organic number now. Thank you.

speaker: Tom Szkutak
title: CFO
content: The second half of the question is that it is organic, so it remains consistent year-over-year. This is the first quarter, and it will be consistent year-over-year. Regarding your question about international growth, we are still experiencing solid growth at 21% on a local currency basis. While there is some softness from a macro standpoint that others mention, it's hard to determine if and how much it affects us, as we are not a bellwether for the economy. Nevertheless, we are pleased with the growth we are observing, with unit growth actually exceeding that rate. In terms of investment, you are correct that we are investing in several regions, including China, where we have been active for several years and will continue to invest. We see it as a great long-term opportunity, and we are currently in investment mode. The recent additions of Italy and Spain are also part of that investment strategy.

speaker: Scott Devitt
title: Analyst
content: Thank you.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: Thank you. Moving on, we will take a question from Mark Mahaney of RBC Capital Markets.

speaker: Mark Mahaney
title: Analyst
content: Thanks for your question. Demand is currently reflecting mid-teens revenue growth on the low end, which has been below the historical average we've experienced. Are there specific factors you want to highlight or refrain from mentioning? Do you believe that the introduction of state sales tax is contributing to a short-term slowdown in growth rates? Last quarter, you mentioned the high-end consumer electronics sector. Are there any specific categories in that sector that might be contributing to the lower end of your growth projections, aside from the negative effects of foreign exchange? Thank you.

speaker: Tom Szkutak
title: CFO
content: Sure. We provide a wide range for our guidance, which we believe is appropriate considering all the factors involved. This practice is not new for us, and we have been doing it for some time. For Q2, our growth rate guidance is between 13% and 26%, recognizing that foreign exchange is impacting this estimate by approximately 275 basis points. On a local currency basis, this translates to approximately 16% to 29%. While it’s a broad range, we believe it accounts for everything necessary as we issue our guidance. The absolute dollar range is quite similar to what we provided for Q1, with perhaps a $100 million difference in the overall value. Once again, we feel that a wide range is appropriate.

speaker: Mark Mahaney
title: Analyst
content: Thank you.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: Our next question today will come from Ben Schachter of Macquarie.

speaker: Ben Schachter
title: Analyst
content: Are there any factors that are impacting the unit growth, particularly the shift from physical to digital, for instance rented video versus purchasing of video? Are there any other factors that you would highlight that are impacting the unit growth?

speaker: Tom Szkutak
title: CFO
content: The overall unit growth is 30% year-over-year, which is solid compared to about 49% in Q1 of last year. We are indeed overlapping a strong growth period from last Q1. In terms of physical versus digital, we are observing that digital is growing at a much faster pace. This is reflected in our third-party units, which make up approximately 40% of total units this quarter, up about 100 basis points from last year. However, since digital units are growing more rapidly, particularly first-party units, the percentage of total units represented by those is not increasing as quickly as in previous quarters. If we focus just on physical units, their share of total units has risen over 300 basis points compared to last year, indicating growth in third-party units as a percentage of total units.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: Our next question today comes from Ross Sandler, Deutsche Bank.

speaker: Ross Sandler
title: Analyst
content: Regarding the follow-up on shipping, the net shipping costs relative to gross profit decreased by about 300 basis points, which is consistent with the trend observed over the past four quarters. As you begin to compare these efficiency gains in shipping, do you believe that this area will continue to show leverage, or do you expect it to stabilize from this point onward?

speaker: Tom Szkutak
title: CFO
content: We are not providing any guidance on specific line items, but over the long term, we believe there is an opportunity for increased productivity and efficiency gains. The team is actively working on this.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: Next, we will hear from Colin Sebastian of Robert W. Baird & Company.

speaker: Colin Sebastian
title: Analyst
content: Just a question on what services you can comment on regarding enterprise-level adoption, and whether there are any significant barriers to that happening over time. We notice you’ve been quite aggressive in hiring enterprise-level salespeople.

speaker: Tom Szkutak
title: CFO
content: No, I don’t think that there is. I think the team has done a fantastic job in terms of developing services that are great for many different customer types, including enterprises. And the team is heads down focused on making sure we have a great operational of these services that are great from an operational standpoint and security standpoint and they are doing a terrific job. And so it’s a very great opportunity for enterprises to adopt our services and the team is certainly focused on that along with other customers. So other customers that took in, it's a great opportunity for those customers and for us.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: Our next question comes from Douglas Anmuth of JPMorgan.

speaker: Douglas Anmuth
title: Analyst
content: You’ve clearly been more aggressive in terms of video content recently and you are sort of leading, was it more in the release tonight in terms of the business content. I was hoping you could just add some more color here on the value that you think TV and movie content adds to consumers’ overall purchase patterns?

speaker: Tom Szkutak
title: CFO
content: Sure. It’s definitely one of our digital offerings, and we provide a range of different services. We have a significant amount of free content included in our prime offer, which we believe is a great service for customers. This is coupled with our express shipping offers and other free content, such as our Kindle Owners Lending Library for books. We consider it to deliver great value to customers as part of our overall value proposition. Additionally, our transaction business for video is performing very well and is growing rapidly, which our customers appreciate. We are seeing this growth reflected in the results presented today.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: Moving on, we will hear from Justin Post with Merrill Lynch. Mr. Post, your line is open. Please go ahead with your question.

speaker: Justin Post
title: Analyst
content: I apologize for that; I was on mute. I wanted to ask about the Kindle ecosystem. In previous calls a few years back, you highlighted it as a rapidly growing area and expressed satisfaction with its performance. We haven't received as much information about it recently. Can you share how unit sales are performing compared to your expectations and the impact it's having on Prime subscriptions as well as your growth in operating margins? Thank you.

speaker: Tom Szkutak
title: CFO
content: We are very pleased with Kindle and the digital business, and we are excited about the ecosystem. This satisfaction is reflected in our results today. For instance, if you examine our media growth, the ecosystem is more established in that area compared to international markets, which is evident in the growth rates associated with them. Additionally, if you look at our top 10 best-selling items worldwide in Q1, all of them are either digital or related to Kindle. The Paperwhite is our best-selling product globally. However, it’s noteworthy that all 10 items in Q1 were either Kindle or digital products. I believe this is the first time we’ve seen such a complete lineup. We have been monitoring quarterly results for some time, and while there have been various combinations in the top 10, this may be the first quarter where every item is either Kindle-related or digital-related. We are very pleased with our progress and will continue to innovate for our customers.

speaker: Justin Post
title: Analyst
content: And any impact on your gross or operating margins you recall?

speaker: Tom Szkutak
title: CFO
content: One thing I would say is we certainly are investing, certainly in the area of investment and you’re seeing that reflected. We are making a number of investments across the business and certainly we are investing in Kindle and our digital offerings. We are investing in some of the things I mentioned earlier like China or some of the emerging geographies. So those are certainly some of the larger key investments we are making.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: Moving on, we will hear from Matt Nemer of Wells Fargo Securities.

speaker: Matt Nemer
title: Analyst
content: Afternoon. We are hearing reports that there is refrigeration equipment going in some of your fulfillment centers outside of the Seattle area. Just wondering if you can update us on plans to expand AmazonFresh. Thanks.

speaker: Tom Szkutak
title: CFO
content: Nothing to announce here. We are very pleased with what we've seen in the Seattle area. But against, it’s been a test and we continue to monitor that test carefully. It’s certainly something that we see that customers love the experience. The challenge has always been in making sure we get the economics right and that is something we will continue to focus on.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: And up next, we will take a question from Steven Ju of Credit Suisse.

speaker: Steven Ju
title: Analyst
content: Hey, Tom, can you provide any insights on how Amazon's video content and your own in-house productions currently contribute to reducing churn in Amazon Prime, and how they might help in the future? Thanks.

speaker: Tom Szkutak
title: CFO
content: Thanks for the question. Yeah. It’s something we haven't released any of the numbers. It’s something that we are tracking very closely. It is something that we believe over time will reduce churn and it’s certainly helping today. What we are seeing is great traction. We see a lot of usage of the service. Customers love it and we think it is a very interesting part of the Prime offering. And that’s why we have been expanding NYC, some of the more recent announcements including some of the stuff included in the earnings release today around original content. So, again, it’s something that we find very interesting and we are excited about it.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: And we will go next to Ken Sena of Evercore Partners with our next question.

speaker: Ken Sena
title: Analyst
content: Hi. I was just hoping you can maybe provide a little more color on the unit growth deceleration. And looking back over the last four quarters, it seems like about 500 basis points or so each quarter of deceleration. You had about 200 basis points here, which is an improvement. But anything you could say just to any signs of maturity in some of the business anywhere that deceleration is specifically coming?

speaker: Tom Szkutak
title: CFO
content: No, there is not a lot I can add. I mean I think the 30% book, very strong growth rate. Again it’s growing at a faster rate than revenue, revenue at 20%, revenue at local currency growth of 24%, a very strong third-party growth continues to be very strong. Retail growth is strong. So again there is not a lot I can provide you there. But again keep in mind that we are overlapping 49% growth last year Q1, which is certainly a little bit of a difficult compare but again fees would be 30% growth rate.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: And our next question today comes from John Blackledge, Cowen & Company.

speaker: John Blackledge
title: Analyst
content: Just a question on the Amazon advertising platform, given the immense number of purchase ads you have on Amazon customers, how is that being used as a competitive advantage and maybe you could just provide an overall view on the direction of the Amazon ad platform over time?

speaker: Tom Szkutak
title: CFO
content: We view the platform as a significant and promising long-term opportunity. We have been dedicating efforts to it for some time, and we find it quite fascinating. You will notice that we are focused on ensuring an excellent customer experience on our site. Our goal is to assist customers in finding and discovering what they want to purchase online. This approach is very customer-focused, while also representing a strong long-term business opportunity with great teams involved. We are enthusiastic about its potential moving forward.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: Moving on to Anthony DiClemente of Barclays.

speaker: Anthony DiClemente
title: Analyst
content: I am curious about the relationship between the attach rate of your transactional video on demand business and the usage of Prime Instant Video. Do consumers typically choose between the two, or does one influence the other? Also, do Prime subscribers have a higher transactional VOD attach rate compared to non-Prime users? I would appreciate hearing your insights on this regarding usage.

speaker: Tom Szkutak
title: CFO
content: I think what's important to note is that Prime customers are engaging with both free and paid content. They are not only accessing free offerings but also purchasing additional content, which we find encouraging. Prime members tend to cross-shop significantly, and it's not unusual for a customer who previously bought in a few categories before joining Prime to increase their purchasing after becoming a member. The same pattern applies to digital content; they often start with free content and then continue to buy paid offerings. This positive trend is one of the reasons we value Prime so highly.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: Up next, we will hear from Youssef Squali of Cantor Fitzgerald.

speaker: Youssef Squali
title: Analyst
content: Two quick questions please. Going back to the international, a question, what’s going on in the international media to decelerate, I think last year Q1 I think it was up 22%, FX adjusted this quarter was up 7%. Is that all macro or are there any maybe other factors that you can talk about, maybe specific to SKUs or something? And the other is more of a clarification. I know last quarter you gave the unit growth in aggregate versus the unit growth of retail, just wondering if you could give that to us as well?

speaker: Tom Szkutak
title: CFO
content: In terms of the international media growth, this quarter it was 1% on a dollar basis, 7% on a local currency basis. In terms of the overall growth rate certainly what you’re seeing is digital content as part of that is growing very fast. But it’s not as large or as penetrated. Our ecosystem isn’t as developed I would say as it is in the U.S. And so when you compare the two geographies for a second that’s one of the more meaningful differences that you see between the two as you see that both are growing digital content very fast. It is just the ecosystem is more built-out in North America. But again, certainly we see very positive signs back in the growth we’re experiencing in international. It’s just on the lower base. So that’s began to be helpful there. In terms of the unit growth, we said that our overall unit growth was 30% for the quarter. Our 3P unit growth, I don’t have the overall growth rate, but it’s growing at a faster rate than the total.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: And our next question today will come from Jordan Rohan of Stifel.

speaker: Jordan Rohan
title: Analyst
content: Yeah. I was hoping you could comment on the market entry and expansion strategy for Amazon in Brazil. There seemed to be a tremendous amount of press last year about it and it seems to have died to some degree. I know the company may already be there with Amazon Web Services and some Kindle offerings. But when do you think that might get a little bit broader? And secondly, there's been some stories recently about an internet streaming device or box or set-top box, something of those sorts. Can you comment on any new hardware form factors including apps as of some sort of a cell phone or handset that might be coming down the pipe, anything to look forward to in the Kindle family or related? Thanks.

speaker: Tom Szkutak
title: CFO
content: Regarding geographic expansion, I can't provide specific details about Brazil. We believe we are currently positioned in the right markets and have expanded into several regions over the past few years. This is an area we continually evaluate, and you can expect us to enter new markets in the future. As for questions about our product roadmap, we have a long-standing practice of not discussing potential plans. However, we are genuinely excited about our future product roadmap and maintain our policy of withholding details until we are closer to launching new offerings.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: And ladies and gentlemen, we do have time for one final question today. That question will come from Jason Helfstein of Oppenheimer & Company.

speaker: Jason Helfstein
title: Analyst
content: Thanks. Can you give us a little more color around customer growth? I mean, that number has been slowing not dramatically, but that is a slowing trend. Are you focused more on higher value customers to drive the business and any color around the quarter would be helpful? Thanks.

speaker: Tom Szkutak
title: CFO
content: We are very pleased with the growth from our customers. We've experienced significant growth, and we have numerous teams across Amazon dedicated to enhancing the customer experience and innovating for our customers. We couldn't be more satisfied with their efforts, which is evident in our overall growth rate this quarter, with revenue increasing by 24% in local currency and units growing by 30%, following a strong growth quarter last year in Q1. Great.

speaker: Sean Boyle
title: Vice President of Investor Relations
content: Thank you for joining us on the call today and for your questions. The reply will be available on our investor relations website at least to the end of the call. We appreciate your interest at Amazon.com and look forward to talking with you again next quarter.

speaker: Sean Boyle
title: VP, Investor Relations
content: Hello and welcome to our Q2 2013 financial results conference call. Joining us today is Tom Szkutak, our CFO. We will be available for questions after our prepared remarks. The following discussion and responses to your questions reflect management's views as of today, July 25, 2013 only and will include forward-looking statements. Actual results may differ materially. Additional information about factors that could potentially impact our financial results is included in today's press release and our filings with the SEC, including our most recent annual report on Form 10-K. As you listen to today’s conference call, we encourage you to have our press release in front of you, which includes our financial results, as well as metrics and commentary on the quarter. During this call, we will discuss certain non-GAAP financial measures. In our press release, slides accompanying this webcast and our filings with the SEC, each of which is posted on our IR website, you will find additional disclosures regarding these non-GAAP measures, including reconciliations of these measures with comparable GAAP measures. Finally, unless otherwise stated, all comparisons in this call will be against our results for the comparable period of 2012. Now, I’ll turn the call over to Tom.

speaker: Thomas J. Szkutak
title: CFO
content: Thanks, Sean. I’ll begin with comments on our second quarter financial results. Trailing 12-month operating cash flow increased 41% to $4.53 billion. Trailing 12-month free cash flow decreased 76% to $265 million. Trailing-12 month capital expenditures were $4.27 billion. This amount includes $1.4 billion in purchases of our previously leased corporate office space, as well as property for development of additional corporate office space located in Seattle, Washington, which we purchased in the fourth quarter of 2012. The increase in capital expenditures reflects additional investments in support of continued business growth consisting of investments in technology, infrastructure including Amazon Web Services and additional capacity to support our fulfillment operations. Return on invested capital was 2%, down from 11%. ROIC is TTM free cash flow divided by average total assets minus current liabilities excluding the current portion of long-term debt over five quarter ends. The combination of common stock and stock-based awards outstanding was 474 million shares compared with 468 million shares. Worldwide revenue grew 22% to $15.7 billion or 25% excluding the $392 million unfavorable impact from year-over-year changes in foreign exchange rates. We are grateful to our customers who continue to take advantage of our low prices, vast selection and shipping offers. Media revenue increased to $4.4 billion, up 7% or 11% excluding foreign exchange. EGM revenue increased to $10.42 billion, up 28% or 30% excluding foreign exchange. Worldwide EGM increased to 66% of worldwide sales, up from 64%. Worldwide paid unit growth was 29%. Active customer accounts exceeded 215 million. Worldwide active seller accounts were more than 2 million. Seller units represented 40% of paid units. Now I will discuss operating expenses, excluding stock-based compensation. Cost of sales was $11.21 billion, or 71.4% of revenue, compared with 73.9%. Fulfillment, marketing, tech and content and G&A combined was $4.09 billion, or 26% of sales, up approximately 275 basis points year-over-year. Fulfillment was $1.76 billion, or 11.2% of revenue compared with 10.1%. Tech and content was $1.43 billion, or 9.1% of revenue, compared with 7.6%. Marketing was $651 million, or 4.1% of revenue consistent with prior period. Now, let’s talk about our segment results, and consistent with prior periods, we do not allocate the segments, our stock-based compensation or other operating expense line item. In the North America segment, revenue grew 30% to $9.49 billion. Media revenue grew 16% to $2.17 billion. EGM revenue grew 31% to $6.48 billion, representing 68% of North America revenues, up from 67%. North America segment operating income increased 19% to $409 million, a 4.3% operating margin. In the international segment, revenue grew 13% to $6.21 billion. Adjusting for the $391 million year-over-year unfavorable foreign exchange impact, revenue growth was 20%. Media revenue decreased 1% to $2.22 billion, or grew 7% excluding foreign exchange, and EGM revenue grew 22% to $3.94 billion, or 29% excluding foreign exchange. EGM now represents 63% of international revenues, up from 59%. International segment operating income was zero, down from $16 million in the prior-year period. Excluding the unfavorable impact from foreign exchange, international segment operating income increased to 11%. CSOI increased 14% to $409 million, or 2.6% of revenue, down approximately 20 basis points year-over-year. Excluding the unfavorable impact from foreign exchange, CSOI increased 19%. Unlike CSOI, our GAAP operating income includes stock-based compensation expense and other operating expense. GAAP operating income decreased 26% to $79 million, or 0.5% of net sales. Our income tax expense was $13 million. GAAP net loss was $7 million or $0.02 per diluted share compared with net income of $7 million and $0.01 per diluted share. Turning to the balance sheet, cash and marketable securities increased $2.49 billion year-over-year to $7.46 billion. Inventory increased 24% to $5.42 billion and inventory turns were 9.4, down from 10.1 turns a year ago as we expanded selection, improved in-stock levels and introduced new product categories. Accounts payable increased 27% to $8.99 billion and accounts payable days increased to 73 from 68 in the prior-year. I’ll conclude my portion of today’s call with guidance. Incorporated into our guidance are the order trends that we’ve seen to date and what we believe today to be appropriately conservative assumptions. Our results are inherently unpredictable and may be materially affected by many factors, including a high level of uncertainty surrounding exchange rate fluctuations, as well as the global economy and consumer spending. It’s not possible to accurately predict demand and therefore our actual results could differ materially from our guidance. As we’ve described in more detail in our public filings, issues such as settling intercompany balances in foreign currencies among our subsidiaries, unfavorable resolution of legal matters and changes to our effective tax rates can all have a material effect on guidance. Our guidance further assumes that we don't conclude any additional business acquisitions, investments, restructurings, or legal settlements, record any further revisions to stock-based compensation estimates and that foreign exchange rates remain approximately where they have been recently. For Q3, 2013, we expect net sales of between $15.45 billion and $17.15 billion, a growth between 12% and 24%. This guidance anticipates approximately 300 basis points of unfavorable impact from foreign exchange rates. GAAP operating loss is expected to be between $440 million and $65 million compared to $28 million in the third quarter of 2012. This includes approximately $340 million of stock-based compensation and amortization of intangible assets. We anticipate consolidated segment operating income or loss, which excludes stock-based compensation and other operating expenses, to be between a $100 million loss and $275 million in income compared to $232 million of income in the third quarter of 2012. We remain heads down focused on driving a better customer experience through price, selection, and convenience. We believe putting customers first is the only reliable way to create lasting value for shareholders. Thanks. And with that, Sean, let’s move to questions.

speaker: Sean Boyle
title: VP, Investor Relations
content: Great. Thanks Tom. Let's move on to the Q&A portion of the call. Operator, will you please remind our listeners how to initiate a question?

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: (Operator Instructions) Our first question comes from Ross Sandler from Deutsche Bank.

speaker: Ross Sandler
title: Analyst, Deutsche Bank
content: Thanks, guys. Just have one question on shipping. It looks like the unit efficiency in shipping continues to improve, what are you guys doing to drive the cost of shipping each unit lower? Are there more costs that can be taken out on a per-unit basis? And then as you start looking at same-day delivery in some of these markets, including the new grocery program, what incremental costs do you see around doing same-day fulfillment? Thanks.

speaker: Thomas J. Szkutak
title: CFO
content: In terms of the economics, we have a great team, operations team that’s working on how we serve customers reliably and faster. So that certainly reflects in our transportation costs. Also from a productivity standpoint, as we add capacity, we’re getting closer and closer to customers with a larger selection which is certainly helpful from a productivity standpoint. So, those are some of the dynamics to think about when you consider our transportation cost and the team has done a great job over the years of becoming even more reliable, faster, and more productive and again we’re working on ways to make that better over time.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: And we’ll move to Douglas Anmuth from JPMorgan.

speaker: Douglas Anmuth
title: Analyst, JPMorgan
content: Great. Thanks for taking my question. I was hoping if you could talk a little bit more just on the profitability of the grocery business and how you’ll know when the right time to expand to more markets beyond Seattle and LA? And then also if you could comment on the European macro environment, just given the growth that you saw in the international business just decelerating a little bit from last quarter? Thanks.

speaker: Thomas J. Szkutak
title: CFO
content: In terms of the fresh business, we started doing the pilot several years ago in Seattle. The team has done a great job inventing on behalf of customers, it’s a very good customer experience. The challenge we’ve had over the past several years is how to make it economically viable. The team has done a lot of different experiments and invented well on behalf of customers to see what works. We took a lot of that knowledge and it enabled us to launch fresh in LA. It’s very early there, and we like what we see so far, but it’s very, very early. It’s something that we’ll continue to work on both from a customer experience and economic standpoint. There isn't much more I can add to that right now, so you have to stay tuned and see where that ends up.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: Our next question comes from Mark Miller from William Blair.

speaker: Mark Miller
title: Analyst, William Blair
content: Hi. Good afternoon. Could you help us understand the third-party unit growth? I think this is the first quarter in about three years that third-party unit penetration hasn’t increased. And then, additionally, I wonder if you could comment at all on potential to expand prime membership options, potentially into something like a super prime offering for expanded video content and fulfillment options?

speaker: Thomas J. Szkutak
title: CFO
content: In terms of the third-party unit growth, it was 40% this quarter, which compares to 40% last year in Q2. So again, it is flat as a percentage of total units. One thing to keep in mind though is our digital units are growing at a faster rate than physical. Those digital units are primarily first-party units. If you take out digital units out in both periods, we’re actually up approximately 300 basis points. The physical seller business is growing very nicely. It’s going at a faster rate than retail, and it’s doing very well, and I’m very pleased to see that.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: And we’ll move now to Brian Pitz from Jefferies.

speaker: Brian Pitz
title: Analyst, Jefferies & Company
content: Great. Thanks. Quick question on fulfillment centers, any color on your current plan for the year in terms of locations, U.S. versus international, timing, etc.? And then separately any comments on the weaker growth in international media? Thanks.

speaker: Thomas J. Szkutak
title: CFO
content: In terms of fulfillment centers, we’ve announced to date five net new facilities in the U.S. We’ve also announced some in international; it’s still early as we did in prior years. We can update you later in the year to see how that progresses. We certainly are adding new capacity, and that’s reflected in the guidance in Q3 as we get ready for our Q4 seasonal quarter. In terms of growth in international media, you're seeing a local currency growth basis, seeing a 7% growth. That’s consistent with what you’ve seen in the last couple of quarters. We’re in the early stages of transformation from physical to digital within international. You’ll see from the release that we’ve launched a lot of new things related to digital over the past 90 days and even prior to that. We’re excited about those launches and the transformation. We also see many opportunities to invest in. I mentioned the conversion from physical to digital. We still have selection to add within existing categories, and we're looking forward to those opportunities.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: We’ll now go to Scott Devitt from Morgan Stanley.

speaker: Scott Devitt
title: Analyst, Morgan Stanley
content: Hi. Thanks. I guess the International topic again, but it has been asked a few times. So maybe specifically in China, Tom, in terms of what the Company hypothesis is regarding the market's evolution over time and how you think about investment spending in that market. And then secondly, as it relates to AWS, it’s nice, the events – the annual event and the quarterly events that happened; I was wondering when you think it makes sense to start talking more about it in releases and on calls? Is it just the 10% revenue threshold or something else that would lead to more discussions on that, on calls like this? Thanks.

speaker: Thomas J. Szkutak
title: CFO
content: In terms of China, we’re investing heavily in China, and we’ve been doing so for a number of years. We have a good customer experience there. We continue to look at ways to improve that. We’re adding selection across many categories right now. It’s a very interesting geography, and we will continue to work on that experience for customers. You should expect us to be in investment mode for some time, but it’s a sizable segment with long-term growth potential, and we’ll keep striving to improve customer and investor experiences over time. In terms of AWS, the business is growing very strongly. We have a great team innovating on behalf of customers, launching new services, becoming more productive, which allows us to lower prices. We’ve had many price reductions since we started with AWS. It’s a big opportunity and we continue to invest in this business.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: Thank you. Our next question comes from Mark Mahaney from RBC.

speaker: Mark Mahaney
title: Analyst, RBC Capital Markets
content: Great. Thanks. Tom, just one question related to consumer packaged goods. Any comments on whether you’re seeing broader purchases by the Amazon customers of more traditional consumer staples than you've seen in the past, and is that something that you’re trying to promote? Thank you.

speaker: Thomas J. Szkutak
title: CFO
content: Yes. To clarify, we’re seeing very good growth across many different categories in our North America growth, particularly in EGM, but if you call out, we’re seeing substantial growth in apparel specifically, and also in consumables. Both teams have done an excellent job from a customer experience standpoint, and they’re growing nicely, which contributes to increased site frequency.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: And we’ll now go to Mark May from Citi.

speaker: Mark May
title: Analyst, Citi
content: Thanks for taking my question. Another one on international in the media segment there. I believe you now have a more comprehensive, localized international strategy for the Kindle. I wonder if you could talk about what impact that might have over the next few quarters in terms of its impact on the international media segment? Also regarding international and AWS; I think one of the contributors of growth and we suspect margins in the U.S. has been the success of AWS here. I wonder if you could share any plans for AWS outside the U.S.?

speaker: Thomas J. Szkutak
title: CFO
content: Sure. In terms of Kindle, you’re right. We now have Kindle stores established in all the Amazon domains globally. We recently announced Kindle Fire HD, which is available to customers in over 170 countries. We introduced Kindle Paperwhite and Kindle Fire HD in China; that’s both online on our website and also in a number of offline retail locations. There’s a lot of advancement around Kindle, but it’s early days. I’m encouraged by the opportunity we have for customers and our potential to capitalize on that from a digital content standpoint. In terms of AWS, the business is expanding, and it’s an incredible opportunity globally. We recognize that, and we’ll continue to see growth on behalf of customers.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: Our next question comes from Justin Post from Merrill Lynch.

speaker: Justin Post
title: Analyst, BofA Merrill Lynch
content: Thank you. The Company and the business are going through a lot of transitions with digital media, AWS, obviously Prime and potentially same-day delivery. Long ago, you used to give us a margin outlook for the Company. As you evaluate these businesses, do you think they’re better suited for Amazon and that you can achieve a greater share of retail as these evolutions take place? Also, what are the implications for Amazon’s long-term margins as you go through these transitions over time? Any insights would be helpful. Thanks.

speaker: Thomas J. Szkutak
title: CFO
content: Sure, in terms of the way we’re looking at it, certainly it is based on free cash flow potential, and we are in some really interesting businesses that have a lot of potential from a free cash flow generation standpoint with good and high ROICs, which is exciting. From a margin standpoint, it’s always challenging to predict where that will come out in terms of absolute numbers. What we aim to do is maximize free cash flow, which has been our consistent goal. People frequently ask us about the potential for double-digit operating margins, and I still think it’s possible; but if a high single-digit operating margin brings us better, higher free cash flow over time, that’s acceptable too. So again, our focus is not on individual margins. Our aim is to ensure that we generate significant free cash flow and use that capital efficiently.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: Our next question comes from Ben Schachter from Macquarie.

speaker: Benjamin Schachter
title: Analyst, Macquarie Securities Group
content: Two quick questions on revenue recognition. Over the past few quarters, I believe that certain digital media has moved around between the agency and wholesale model. Can you help us quantify how this has actually impacted the reported media revenue rates? In other words, would 2Q revenue rates have been meaningfully different if the model had been consistent? And then the second question, just quickly on Prime; can you remind us how you recognized revenue from the Prime memberships deal over the course of the year? Thanks.

speaker: Thomas J. Szkutak
title: CFO
content: Sure. In terms of the Prime revenue, we recognized it over the life of the subscription. In terms of third-party versus first-party, there has indeed been a shift within digital media, but remember that digital media is primarily a first-party business and it constitutes just one part of our overall operation. You’re correct, and regarding our third-party business, which made up about 40% of our total units this quarter, we recognized the share of revenue, the ad revenue where the other parts of the business were largely recognized as first-party revenue, and so we’ve captured the full amount of revenue in the current period.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: Thank you. Our next question comes from Jordan Rohan from Stifel, Nicolaus.

speaker: Jordan Rohan
title: Analyst, Stifel, Nicolaus & Company
content: Thank you so much. I’m curious about your expansion efforts in Spain since it's a relatively new territory for you, how well situated you are and how ready you are for the fourth quarter there? There have been many stories about Amazon heading into Brazil, but I don’t believe we’ve identified any fulfillment centers and things like that. Can you discuss the extent and breadth of your offering in Brazil, whether it's Kindle devices, digital media or something beyond that? Thank you.

speaker: Thomas J. Szkutak
title: CFO
content: In terms of Spain, we’re very excited about what we see. It's growing very fast. We’re in investment mode and it's an exciting geography. We’re optimistic that over time it will become a strong market for us. We’re very happy to serve customers in Spain, and we’re continuing to expand our selection and improve service levels as we go. In terms of Brazil, we do have a Kindle store and we have devices at physical retailers, so from a Kindle perspective that’s what we’re doing in Brazil.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: Our next question comes from Ron Josey from JMP Securities.

speaker: Ronald Josey
title: Analyst, JMP Securities
content: Thank you for taking my question. I'm curious about North America EGM. Given the strong performance of the business and its ongoing growth, have you noticed any impact from price matching programs by offline retailers or from sales tax? Thank you.

speaker: Thomas J. Szkutak
title: CFO
content: In terms of North America, total growth, we saw an acceleration from last quarter from 26% to 30%. We saw growth acceleration in both North American Media and North America EGM. Within EGM it was broad; we saw strong growth across many different categories. I’m very pleased with that, notably in apparel and consumables, both of which are growing quickly. In terms of competitiveness, it's a very competitive landscape. It’s been this way since our inception, whether we're talking about competitors online or offline. Every day, as you go home or work, you pass our competitors, and that’s something we're used to dealing with.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: Our next question comes from Heath Terry from Goldman Sachs.

speaker: Heath Terry
title: Analyst, Goldman Sachs
content: Great, thank you Tom. As you get closer to customers with more fulfillment centers and more efficient shipping, what kind of impact is that having on conversion rates within those areas as shipping and delivery times shorten? As you look at early adopters for Fresh in LA, can you share any insights on what kind of cross-shopping you’re seeing among new Fresh customers? Are they bundling media and EGM in those other orders, or to any degree are these new Amazon customers who were brought in purely because of Fresh?

speaker: Thomas J. Szkutak
title: CFO
content: If you take a look at LA, I’m very excited, but it’s very early. I think you’ll just have to stay tuned on that. In terms of, as we get closer to customers with fulfillment, we have seen growth due to that. It’s shown up in several different ways, but notably you’ll see it in Prime. Because of our fulfillment logistics capability, we’ve been able to broaden our Prime offerings, and we continue to expand selection so it’s becoming more accessible to customers. Over the last several years, we’ve encountered different reasons for our growth, and we’ve procured larger selections at sharp prices, but certainly Prime services, which includes speedy delivery, have had a remarkable impact. Customer feedback on the Prime program is positive; we’re seeing strong growth in Prime subscribers and high retention rates among those members. It’s a fantastic program for us.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: Our next question comes from Anthony Diclemente from Barclays.

speaker: Anthony Diclemente
title: Analyst, Barclays Capital
content: Thank you. On the topic of media, I was wondering if there are any specifics in terms of categories of strength or weakness within physical or digital media that you might want to share. Along those lines, I’m curious about your media device rollout strategy from here. Is there any reason PrimeInstant Video isn’t available for Android devices? Thank you.

speaker: Thomas J. Szkutak
title: CFO
content: In terms of media growth, not a lot of specifics except for the obvious - digital units are growing very quickly compared to physical units and we’re pleased with that. We’re further penetrated in North America, which is resulting in a greater growth impact than in international. There are many factors at play, and in our release, you’ll see specific numbers related to our offerings, and there are many different elements working together in that space as part of our digital ecosystem, which we’re happy with. Regarding our device strategy, we’re excited about our device offerings and believe we have a fantastic lineup in terms of Kindle and Kindle Fire devices. As for our future roadmap, we have a long-standing practice of not discussing future products before they are officially announced.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: Our next question comes from Youssef Squali from Cantor Fitzgerald.

speaker: Youssef Squali
title: Analyst, Cantor Fitzgerald
content: Thank you very much, two quick questions. Tech and content were up to 9% of revenues, I think that’s the highest it's ever been. How much of that is actually streaming content related, and how do we look at that going forward? Does it stay at that elevated level? And then on Fresh, is that business profitable for you in the Seattle area? Thanks.

speaker: Thomas J. Szkutak
title: CFO
content: In terms of tech and content, we're spending in numerous areas, but I'd like to highlight a few. One is certainly the infrastructure related to our rapidly growing web services business, which is included in tech and content expenses. speaker: Cindy McCann
title: Vice President of Investor Relations
content: Good afternoon, and thank you for joining us. On today’s call are John Mackey and Walter Robb, Co-Chief Executive Officers, A.C. Gallo, President, Jim Sud, Executive Vice President of Growth & Development, and David Lannon and Ken Meyer, Executive Vice Presidents of Operations. As a reminder, all forward-looking statements on this call are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from the expectations and assumptions discussed today. This may be due to a variety of factors, including the risks outlined in our company’s most recently filed Form 10-K. Please note, our press release and scripted remarks are available on our website. We assume you have read our press release, so we will use this time to focus on highlights from the quarter as well as our future outlook. All references to shares outstanding and per share amounts are adjusted to reflect our two-for-one stock split on May 29. I will now turn the call over to Walter Robb.

speaker: Walter Robb
title: Co-Chief Executive Officer
content: Thank you, Cindy, and good afternoon, everyone. We are very pleased to deliver another outstanding quarter. We produced a 20% increase in earnings per share on a 12% increase in sales, once again reporting a record or near record results on many levels, including average weekly sales per store of $728,000, translating to sales per gross square foot of $996, gross margin of 36.6%, store contribution of 11%, operating margin of 7.5%, EBITDA margin of 10%, and a return on invested capital of 16.5%. Our solid performance and capital discipline generated $228 million in operating cash flow. We invested $115 million in new and existing stores resulting in $133 million in free cash flow. In addition, we repurchased $25 million of stock and returned $37 million in dividends to our shareholders. We ended the quarter with $1.5 billion in cash and investments and $384 million in share repurchase authority. Our sales trends have remained consistent over the last three quarters. For Q3, excluding an estimated 45 basis points, a positive impact from our Team Member Appreciation Double Discount Day, our identical store sales increased 6.7%, or 15.3% on a two-year basis. The increase was driven by an approximate 4% increase in transaction count and a 3% increase in basket size. Our sales momentum and operating disciplines, along with moderating inflation, helped generate another quarter of record gross margin performance. We remain committed to expanding our value offerings across the store, increasing our promotional activity and improving our relative price positioning. We continue to be very competitive in non-perishables with more opportunities to narrow the gap in perishables which reflect our higher quality standards. This quarter, our value efforts were more than offset by occupancy leverage, shrink reduction, and buy-side initiatives. In addition, the cost of goods sold was positively impacted 19 basis points by a decrease in wholesale revenue related to our meat procurement program. Excluding this, our gross margin was 36.4%, in line with the second quarter. Direct store expenses increased 27 basis points to 25.6% of sales. Excluding the negative impact of the decrease in wholesale revenue and increase in team member discount costs related to our Double Discount Day, our direct store expenses as a percentage of sales were in line with our Q2 results of 25.4%. Store contribution was 11% of sales, in line with our record Q2 results. We opened four stores this quarter, expanding into three new markets. We are able to enter markets as diverse as suburban Danbury, Connecticut, to urban Detroit, Michigan by tailoring our store size, product selection and pricing strategy to the particular community. In Detroit, we implemented a new value strategy in our perishable areas that has been very well received. We are opening a similar store in New Orleans later this year, and we think that there's opportunities to duplicate elements of this value strategy for perishables in select markets across the country. Our new stores are continuing to deliver very healthy returns. For the last eight quarters, on average, our new store class has consisted of 26 stores open for approximately six months. At 37,000 square feet in size, they have produced average weekly sales of $528,000, translating to sales per gross square foot of $745, and generated a 5% contribution margin. These results, combined with our capital investment and pre-opening expense discipline, enabled us to deliver another quarter of high return on invested capital. For the quarter, our 25 comparable stores less than two years old produced an after-tax return on invested capital of 19%, another Q3 record. Check out the beyond-the-numbers section of our investor relations webpage for additional information about our new stores and more. Turning now to our updated outlook for the fiscal year and initial outlook for fiscal '14. Based on our strong Q3 results and our updated assumptions for the fourth quarter, we have raised our fiscal 2013 diluted EPS outlook by $0.01 to $0.02. Our new fiscal year EPS range of $1.45 to $1.46 implies EPS of $0.30 to $0.31 for Q4. As we typically do at this point in the year, we are also narrowing our fiscal year ranges for comps and idents based on our year-to-date results. Our idents for the first three weeks of Q4 are 5.5%, which we attribute primarily to a tough comparison of 9.5% in the prior year. Our guidance for the quarter is 6.5% to 7%, or 14.8% to 15.3% on a two-year basis. This guidance reflects an expected acceleration in idents over the last nine weeks of Q4 as our year-ago comparison eases 150 basis points to 8%. The high end of the two-year range is consistent with our Q3 results excluding the positive impact from our Double Discount Day. Regarding gross margin, our long-term strategy remains in place. We are continuing to implement various value efforts, including more aggressive price matching against select competitors. We have been successful at offsetting these efforts thus far, but are not expecting the same degree of leverage in Q4. We also want to remind investors that our average weekly sales and gross profit as a percentage of sales are typically highest in the second and third quarters and lowest in the fourth quarter due to seasonally slower sales during the summer months. On a 12-week to 12-week basis, we expect operating income before pre-opening to increase a healthy 16% to 20% in Q4. We expect a record 12 new store openings versus seven last year, as well as a high number of openings in Q1 of next year, to drive a significant year-over-year increase in pre-opening expense and lower EPS growth of 7% to 11% compared to the 20% we produced year-to-date. Our initial outlook for fiscal year 2014 reflects another great year of consistent sales growth, record new store openings, and strong operational performance. We expect sales growth of 12% to 14%, comps of 6.5% to 8%, idents of 6% to 7.5%, and an EPS growth of 17% to 18%. This is an exciting time for our company. We are dedicated to providing communities with fresh, healthy, natural, and organic food and are on track to deliver our fourth consecutive year of increases in new store openings. We continue to gain market share and see demand for 1,000 Whole Foods Market stores in the U.S. alone. Our outstanding operational performance is funding our growth, and our new stores are creating a cycle of innovation across the company. We have signed 50 new leases over the last 12 months and now have 94 signed leases, nearly a three-year supply of new stores in the pipeline. We expect accelerating square footage growth for several years to come. Each week, over seven million customers visit our 355 stores in 40 states and three countries. We are confident we can maintain our leadership position and continue to gain market share as we step up our new store openings, improve our relative value proposition, further differentiate our shopping experience, and reinforce our standing as America's healthiest grocery store. We will now take questions. Please limit yourself to one question at a time so that everyone has an opportunity to participate. Our call will end at 4:30 Central Time. Thank you.

Your other question was around the basket. Do you guys want to comment on the basket? It's all about the average price, really. Do you want to comment on the basket composition at all? What we are seeing on units or pricing on anything there?

speaker: David Lannon
title: Executive Vice President of Operations
content: Well, I think in the third quarter, we have done a really good job of being clear about how we market price and being very surgical about we price and where we want to put the value, where we want to make investments, and that’s definitely showing up in how the basket composition has changed. Also, the various one-day deals and weekend deals that we have, that’s affected as well and that isn’t consistent year-over-year, it varies with what we have available to us and what we promote at the time. So that all factors in how the basket evolves.

speaker: Walter Robb
title: Co-Chief Executive Officer
content: Are we getting extra question?

speaker: Shane Higgins
title: Analyst
content: Yes, I think so. That’s helpful. Are you guys pulling in new shoppers you think as well? You mentioned the promotions that you guys have been running. Do you think that’s also attracting people outside your core loyal customers?

speaker: David Lannon
title: Executive Vice President of Operations
content: Yes, we are (indiscernible) by the trade. This is David. As the Detroit experience, again, it hasn’t been a core demographic of Whole Foods Market. So, we are thrilled and our stores are doing at least double of what we expected it to do, and it's off to a tremendous start and it has super diverse customer base. Again, we think that gives us great confidence to go into markets we haven’t been or people haven’t thought of as traditional for Whole Foods Market at best.

speaker: Walter Robb
title: Co-Chief Executive Officer
content: I think the other thing you mentioned is, I don’t know if you noticed but our social media presence is almost 3 million and 4 million twitter. We are number two brand on Twitter and I think that allows us to bridge into a new generation of customers who are digital natives, and it creates us another exciting platform for us to reach people. So, yes, I do think we are generating new customers. I would like to be able to give you a more scientific answer on that but just that sort of platform, that sort of ability to reach people is really helping us.

speaker: Operator
title: Operator
content: Thank you. We will take our final question today from Robert Ohmes with Bank of America. Your line is open.

speaker: Robert Ohmes
title: Analyst
content: I just had a follow-up question on the comment about, I think Walter you might have made it on more aggressive price matching against select competitors. I was hoping maybe you could talk a little bit about whether that is more targeted towards natural organic competitors or the traditional groceries? Also, is it pretty regionalized or is it broad by category or is it targeted to the produce category? Maybe just a little more color about that more aggressive price matching that you guys are doing now. Thanks.

speaker: Ken Meyer
title: Executive Vice President of Operations
content: This is Ken here. I think what we are looking at with pricing is it depends upon the market. We look at primary competitors. So it could be a traditional or conventional competitor, it could be a natural food competitor, it could be a rising competitor that’s new into the marketplace. So it very much depends upon who we see as the folks that we want to compete against and price against, and so we study that. We look at how we want to match up, what categories are we going to look at, what the pricing are going to look like, and so it’s a very comprehensive process that varies, even store-to-store, but market-to-market, and we feel really good that the data that we have and the methodology which we are using now is stronger than ever. It does give us the ability to promote differently and merchandise the stores differently based on value. Want to speak some more?

speaker: David Lannon
title: Executive Vice President of Operations
content: And we also, our data team is at a point now where we have such good information that we do a lot of experiments that’s just really exciting. So we can try a lot of different pricing initiatives against different types of competitors, again in different marketplaces with different products and see what happens. See what kind of elasticity there is in terms of the pricing versus pickup in sales and see what the customers really want. So we are doing a lot of that kind of experimenting and it's a whole new area for us. It is not something that we have really had the types of data and the team that we worked on before. Some of the experimental data really have been spearheading. I find it very exciting.

speaker: Ken Meyer
title: Executive Vice President of Operations
content: Our team members are very proud of our prices. We don’t have to be ashamed compared to any other competitors because we have competitive prices and we are proud to show you about it and show it in our stores.
